1.206.s:
.. bhīṣma uvāca .. ..
maṃtroddhāraṃ paraṃ brūhi mudrāśaktisamanvitam ..
rūpavarṇa samaṃ caiva paurāṇikamanuttamam .. 1 ..
1.206.d:
॥ भीष्म उवाच ॥ ॥
मंत्रोद्धारं परं ब्रूहि मुद्राशक्तिसमन्वितम् ॥
रूपवर्ण समं चैव पौराणिकमनुत्तमम् ॥ 1 ॥
1.206.m:
Bhīṣma said:
Tell me the supreme extraction of mantras, accompanied by mudrās and śaktis, / matching form and color, the unexcelled Purāṇic [lore].

1.206.s:
.. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu bhīṣma mahābāho yathā vakṣyāmi tenagha ..
paurāṇikānāṃ maṃtrāṇāmuddhāraṃ vaidikādṛte ..2..
1.206.d:
॥ व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणु भीष्म महाबाहो यथा वक्ष्यामि तेनघ ॥
पौराणिकानां मंत्राणामुद्धारं वैदिकादृते ॥2॥
1.206.m:
Vyāsa said:
Listen, O mighty-armed Bhīṣma, as I shall speak to you, O sinless one, / concerning the extraction of Purāṇic mantras, apart from the Vedic [ones].

1.206.s:
varṇarephasamāyuktaṃ vidrumenaiva bhūṣitam ..
aṃtasthānāṃ hi aṃtyaṃ vai brahmadaivatyamucyate ..3..
1.206.d:
वर्णरेफसमायुक्तं विद्रुमेनैव भूषितम् ॥
अंतस्थानां हि अंत्यं वै ब्रह्मदैवत्यमुच्यते ॥3॥
1.206.m: Joined with the letter r and adorned with coral, / the last of the semivowels is said to have Brahmā as its deity.

1.206.s:
biṃdurephasamāyuktaṃ dīrghayā mātrayā tathā ..
dīkṣākṣaraṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ dvitīyaṃ viṣṇudaivatam ..4..
1.206.d:
बिंदुरेफसमायुक्तं दीर्घया मात्रया तथा ॥
दीक्षाक्षरं समुद्दिष्टं द्वितीयं विष्णुदैवतम् ॥4॥
1.206.m: Endowed with the bindu and the letter r, and likewise with a long vowel-measure, / the syllable of initiation is declared; the second has Viṣṇu as its deity.

1.206.s:
tṛtīyaṃ tu tathā proktaṃ savisargaṃ janādhipa ..
sa tṛtīyo budhaiḥ prokto rudradaivata eva hi ..5..
1.206.d:
तृतीयं तु तथा प्रोक्तं सविसर्गं जनाधिप ॥
स तृतीयो बुधैः प्रोक्तो रुद्रदैवत एव हि ॥5॥
1.206.m: The third is likewise proclaimed, O ruler of men, as having a visarga; / that third is indeed declared by the wise to have Rudra as its deity.

1.206.s:
bhāskaroyaṃ mahānsākṣānmaṃtramūrtistrirakṣaraḥ..
durlabhaḥ paramo guhyastridevo devapūjitaḥ ..6..
1.206.d:
भास्करोयं महान्साक्षान्मंत्रमूर्तिस्त्रिरक्षरः॥
दुर्लभः परमो गुह्यस्त्रिदेवो देवपूजितः ॥6॥
1.206.m: This is the great Sun, directly the embodiment of the mantra, possessing three syllables, / difficult to attain, supremely secret, the threefold deity, worshipped by the gods.

1.206.s:
yastvidaṃ japate bhaktyā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ..
tataśca mudrāṃ vakṣyāmi sānnidhya kāraṇaṃ param ..7..
1.206.d:
यस्त्विदं जपते भक्त्या स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
ततश्च मुद्रां वक्ष्यामि सान्निध्य कारणं परम् ॥7॥
1.206.m: He who recites this with devotion goes to the supreme state. / And next I will speak of the mudrā, the supreme cause of [divine] presence.

1.206.s:
padmākārau karau kṛtvā madhye śliṣṭe tu madhyame..
aṃguliṃ kṣārayettasminvimudreti ca socyate ..8..
1.206.d:
पद्माकारौ करौ कृत्वा मध्ये श्लिष्टे तु मध्यमे॥
अंगुलिं क्षारयेत्तस्मिन्विमुद्रेति च सोच्यते ॥8॥
1.206.m: Having made the hands in the shape of a lotus, with the middle fingers joined in the middle, / one should extend the finger upon it; this is called the Vimudrā.

1.206.s:
anayā baddhayā rājanbhāskarasya priyo bhavet ..
mahābhayeṣu sarveṣu mātṛvatparirakṣati .. 9 ..
1.206.d:
अनया बद्धया राजन्भास्करस्य प्रियो भवेत् ॥
महाभयेषु सर्वेषु मातृवत्परिरक्षति ॥ 9 ॥
1.206.m: When this [mudrā] is bound, O king, one becomes dear to the Sun; / in all great perils, he protects [one] like a mother.

1.206.s:
hṛdayaṃ tasya vijñeyaṃ yadakṣaravaraṃ smṛtam ..
vidrumopari saṃchannaṃ hṛdgataṃ tadgataṃ sadā .. 10 ..
1.206.d:
हृदयं तस्य विज्ञेयं यदक्षरवरं स्मृतम् ॥
विद्रुमोपरि संछन्नं हृद्गतं तद्गतं सदा ॥ 10 ॥
1.206.m: His heart is to be known as that which is remembered as the excellent syllable / covered over the coral, residing in the heart, ever directed to it.

1.206.s:
śirasyarkamiti proktaṃ devadevasya bhārata ..
mahāvyāhṛtayastisrastathārajvālinī śikhā .. 11 ..
1.206.d:
शिरस्यर्कमिति प्रोक्तं देवदेवस्य भारत ॥
महाव्याहृतयस्तिस्रस्तथारज्वालिनी शिखा ॥ 11 ॥
1.206.m: "Arka" is proclaimed for the head of the god of gods, O descendant of Bharata; / the three great vyāhṛtis, and likewise the lock of hair is Arciṣmatī.

1.206.s:
aṣṭākṣarā tu vidyeyamādityasya mahātmanaḥ ..
yaḥ smaretsādhakastvenaṃ nāsau kenāpi bādhyate .. 12 ..
1.206.d:
अष्टाक्षरा तु विद्येयमादित्यस्य महात्मनः ॥
यः स्मरेत्साधकस्त्वेनं नासौ केनापि बाध्यते ॥ 12 ॥
1.206.m: This is the eight-syllabled spell of the great-souled Sun. / The practitioner who remembers it is not afflicted by anything.

1.206.s:
akāreṇa samāyuktaṃ biṃdurephasamanvitam ..
hakāramagnidaivatyaṃ kavacaṃ bhāskarapriyam.. 13 ..
1.206.d:
अकारेण समायुक्तं बिंदुरेफसमन्वितम् ॥
हकारमग्निदैवत्यं कवचं भास्करप्रियम्॥ 13 ॥
1.206.m: Joined with the letter a, endowed with bindu and the letter r, / the letter ha has Agni as its deity; [it is] the armor dear to the Sun.

1.206.s:
ekākṣaramidaṃ proktamabhedyaṃ yaḥ smaredidam ..
duṣṭānāṃ caiva vighnānāṃ nāśanaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 14 ..
1.206.d:
एकाक्षरमिदं प्रोक्तमभेद्यं यः स्मरेदिदम् ॥
दुष्टानां चैव विघ्नानां नाशनं नात्र संशयः ॥ 14 ॥
1.206.m: This is declared to be of one syllable, impenetrable; he who remembers this— / it destroys wicked obstacles, there is no doubt of this.

1.206.s:
savisargo repha iti astramekākṣaraṃ smṛtam ..
nāśayedduṣṭakarmāṇi sādhakasya na saṃśayaḥ .. 15 ..
1.206.d:
सविसर्गो रेफ इति अस्त्रमेकाक्षरं स्मृतम् ॥
नाशयेद्दुष्टकर्माणि साधकस्य न संशयः ॥ 15 ॥
1.206.m: The letter r with a visarga is remembered as the one-syllabled weapon; / it destroys the wicked deeds of the practitioner, there is no doubt.

1.206.s:
saṃmukhau tau karau kṛtvā śliṣṭau tu grathitāṃgulī ..
kaniṣṭhenāmike yojye tarjanyau madhyame tathā .. .. 16 ..
1.206.d:
संमुखौ तौ करौ कृत्वा श्लिष्टौ तु ग्रथितांगुली ॥
कनिष्ठेनामिके योज्ये तर्जन्यौ मध्यमे तथा ॥ ॥ 16 ॥
1.206.m: Having brought the two hands face to face, joined with fingers interlaced, / the little fingers and ring fingers should be joined, and likewise the forefingers and middle fingers.

1.206.s:
hṛcchiraḥ saśikhā carmā mudreyaṃ vyomasaṃjñitā ..
muṣṭivakrocchritaṃ kuryātsavyahastasya tarjanīm ..17..
1.206.d:
हृच्छिरः सशिखा चर्मा मुद्रेयं व्योमसंज्ञिता ॥
मुष्टिवक्रोच्छ्रितं कुर्यात्सव्यहस्तस्य तर्जनीम् ॥17॥
1.206.m: Pertaining to heart, head, tuft, and armor, this mudrā is called Vyoma. / One should make a fist and raise the forefinger of the right hand curved:

1.206.s:
mālaśabdakṛtādistu mudrā hyastrasya kīrtitā ..
trāsanī nāma vikhyātā sarvaviprabhayaṃkarī .. 18 ..
1.206.d:
मालशब्दकृतादिस्तु मुद्रा ह्यस्त्रस्य कीर्तिता ॥
त्रासनी नाम विख्याता सर्वविप्रभयंकरी ॥ 18 ॥
1.206.m: beginning with the sound of a garland, it is celebrated as the mudrā of the weapon, / renowned by the name Trāsanī, inspiring terror in all adversaries.

1.206.s:
karṇabiṃdusamāyuktaṃ yaṃ caturthaṃ mahāmate ..
bhāskarasya tvidaṃ netramagridaivatamucyate ... .. 19 ..
1.206.d:
कर्णबिंदुसमायुक्तं यं चतुर्थं महामते ॥
भास्करस्य त्विदं नेत्रमग्रिदैवतमुच्यते ॥॥। 19 ॥
1.206.m: The fourth [semivowel] endowed with the ear-vowel and bindu, O highly intelligent one, / is said to be this eye of the Sun, having Agni as its deity.

1.206.s:
smaraḥ syātsādhakeṃdrāṇāṃ duraṃto nāśane dhruvam ..
madhyamā tarjanī caiva savyahastasya cocchritam.. 20 ..
1.206.d:
स्मरः स्यात्साधकेंद्राणां दुरंतो नाशने ध्रुवम् ॥
मध्यमा तर्जनी चैव सव्यहस्तस्य चोच्छ्रितम्॥ 20 ॥
1.206.m: Smara would certainly bring endless destruction to the best of practitioners. / The middle and index fingers of the right hand are raised,

1.206.s:
kaniṣṭhānāmike kuṃcya aṃguṣṭhena tataḥ kramet ..
netrābhyāṃ sparśayedenāṃ netramudrā prakīrtitā .. 21 ..
1.206.d:
कनिष्ठानामिके कुंच्य अंगुष्ठेन ततः क्रमेत् ॥
नेत्राभ्यां स्पर्शयेदेनां नेत्रमुद्रा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 21 ॥
1.206.m: and bending the little and ring fingers, one should then touch with the thumb / and touch the eyes with it; this is proclaimed as the eye-mudrā.

1.206.s:
govṛṣā nāma vikhyātā darśayeddivyagocaram ..
rāṃ dīptāriṃ tataḥ sūkṣmārīṃ jayā bhīṣma ucyate .. 22 ..
1.206.d:
गोवृषा नाम विख्याता दर्शयेद्दिव्यगोचरम् ॥
रां दीप्तारिं ततः सूक्ष्मारीं जया भीष्म उच्यते ॥ 22 ॥
1.206.m: Renowned by the name Govṛṣā, it reveals the divine sphere. / "Rāṃ" is Dīptā, "rīṃ" then is Sūkṣmā, "jayā" is spoken of, O Bhīṣma,

1.206.s:
ubhāhvārūṃ vibhūtiśca vimalā reṃ prakīrtitā ..
aghahā ca mahābāho vidyutā rauṃ prakīrtitā .. 23 ..
1.206.d:
उभाह्वारूं विभूतिश्च विमला रें प्रकीर्तिता ॥
अघहा च महाबाहो विद्युता रौं प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 23 ॥
1.206.m: "rūṃ" is called both [Bhadrakarī] and Vibhūti, "reṃ" is proclaimed as Vimalā, / and "raiṃ" is Aghahā, O mighty-armed one; "rauṃ" is proclaimed as Vidyutā,

1.206.s:
govṛṣā nāma raṃ sarvaṃ vīrabhadrakarī tathā ..
ityetā bījarūpāstu kathitāścaiva śaktayaḥ .. 24 ..
1.206.d:
गोवृषा नाम रं सर्वं वीरभद्रकरी तथा ॥
इत्येता बीजरूपास्तु कथिताश्चैव शक्तयः ॥ 24 ॥
1.206.m: "raṃ" is Govṛṣā, all [these], and likewise Vīrabhadrakarī. / Thus these śaktis have been proclaimed in the form of seed-syllables.

1.206.s:
uttānau tu karau kṛtvā savyākuṃcya tatoṃgulīḥ ..
kuryādupari cāṃguṣṭhau cālayeta punaḥpunaḥ .. 25 ..
1.206.d:
उत्तानौ तु करौ कृत्वा सव्याकुंच्य ततोंगुलीः ॥
कुर्यादुपरि चांगुष्ठौ चालयेत पुनःपुनः ॥ 25 ॥
1.206.m: Having placed the hands facing upward and then bent the fingers inwards, / one should place the thumbs above and move them again and again.

1.206.s:
sarvāsāṃ caiva śaktīnāmetā mudrāḥ pradarśayet ..
nāmnā ca vidyutā caiva navamī sarvatomukhī .. 26 ..
1.206.d:
सर्वासां चैव शक्तीनामेता मुद्राः प्रदर्शयेत् ॥
नाम्ना च विद्युता चैव नवमी सर्वतोमुखी ॥ 26 ॥
1.206.m: One should display these mudrās for all the śaktis; / by name, the ninth is Vidyutā, facing in all directions.

1.206.s:
nāmānyetāni śaktīnāṃ samāsātkathitāni tu ..
sabījāni mahābāho mayā snehena bhārata .. 27 ..
1.206.d:
नामान्येतानि शक्तीनां समासात्कथितानि तु ॥
सबीजानि महाबाहो मया स्नेहेन भारत ॥ 27 ॥
1.206.m: These names of the śaktis have been spoken briefly / together with their seed-syllables by me out of affection, O mighty-armed Bhārata.

1.206.s:
grahāṇāṃ śṛṇu bījāni rūpaṃ ca gadato mama ..
sarvatra bhaṃ tathā khaṃ ca kaṃjakūtuhalodvaha .. 28 ..
1.206.d:
ग्रहाणां शृणु बीजानि रूपं च गदतो मम ॥
सर्वत्र भं तथा खं च कंजकूतुहलोद्वह ॥ 28 ॥
1.206.m: Hear from me as I speak the seed-syllables of the planets and their form: / everywhere "bhaṃ" and "khaṃ", O bearer of curiosity for the lotus[-born],

1.206.s:
oṃkārā dīpitāḥ sarve namaskārāṃtayojitāḥ ..
pūjākāle prayoktavyā japakāle tathaiva ca .. 29 ..
1.206.d:
ओंकारा दीपिताः सर्वे नमस्कारांतयोजिताः ॥
पूजाकाले प्रयोक्तव्या जपकाले तथैव च ॥ 29 ॥
1.206.m: all illuminated by the syllable Oṃ and joined with "namas" at the end, / are to be employed at the time of worship and likewise at the time of recitation.

1.206.s:
homakāle tu svāhāṃtaṃ maṃtraṃ ṣaṭkārasaṃyutam ..
sarve biṃduyutā bhīṣma śikhā biṃduvibhūṣitāḥ .. 30 ..
1.206.d:
होमकाले तु स्वाहांतं मंत्रं षट्कारसंयुतम् ॥
सर्वे बिंदुयुता भीष्म शिखा बिंदुविभूषिताः ॥ 30 ॥
1.206.m: At the time of oblations, however, the mantra ends in "svāhā" and is joined with the six syllables. / All are endowed with a bindu, O Bhīṣma, and the crests are adorned with a bindu.

1.206.s:
somādyāḥ ketuparyaṃtā grahā hyevaṃ prakīrtitāḥ ..
etā mudrāḥ pravakṣyāmi sarvasiddhipradāyikāḥ .. 31 ..
1.206.d:
सोमाद्याः केतुपर्यंता ग्रहा ह्येवं प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
एता मुद्राः प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वसिद्धिप्रदायिकाः ॥ 31 ॥
1.206.m: Thus the planets beginning with Soma and ending with Ketu are proclaimed. / I shall declare these mudrās that bestow all attainments.

1.206.s:
sumukhau tu karau kṛtvā śliṣṭau caiva prasāritau ..
iyaṃ mudrā namaskāre grahasānnidhyakārikā .. .. 32 ..
1.206.d:
सुमुखौ तु करौ कृत्वा श्लिष्टौ चैव प्रसारितौ ॥
इयं मुद्रा नमस्कारे ग्रहसान्निध्यकारिका ॥ ॥ 32 ॥
1.206.m: Having made the hands well-formed, joined, and stretched out, / this mudrā in reverent salutation effects the presence of the planets.

1.206.s:
maṃtroddhārastavākhyāto rahasyo durlabho nṛpa ..
śṛṇuṣva rūpaṃ devānāṃ dhyānakāle hyupasthite .. 33 ..
1.206.d:
मंत्रोद्धारस्तवाख्यातो रहस्यो दुर्लभो नृप ॥
शृणुष्व रूपं देवानां ध्यानकाले ह्युपस्थिते ॥ 33 ॥
1.206.m: The extraction of mantras, secret and hard to obtain, has been told to you, O king. / Hear the form of the deities when the time for meditation has arrived:

1.206.s:
japāvarṇaṃ mahātejaṃ śvetapadmopari sthitam..
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam .. 34 ..
1.206.d:
जपावर्णं महातेजं श्वेतपद्मोपरि स्थितम्॥
सर्वलक्षणसंपन्नं सर्वाभरणभूषितम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.206.m: having the colour of a hibiscus flower, possessing great splendour, seated upon a white lotus, / endowed with all auspicious marks, adorned with all ornaments,

1.206.s:
tathaikavaktraṃ dvibhujaṃ somapaṃkajakaṃdharam ..
maṃḍalena ca rūpaṃ tu madhyasthaṃ raktavāsasam .. 35 ..
1.206.d:
तथैकवक्त्रं द्विभुजं सोमपंकजकंधरम् ॥
मंडलेन च रूपं तु मध्यस्थं रक्तवाससम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.206.m: having one face, two arms, a neck like a soma-lotus, / whose form stands within the disc, dressed in red garments.

1.206.s:
mārtaṃḍasya idaṃ rūpaṃ śuciḥ snāto jiteṃdriyaḥ..
trikālaṃ yaḥ smaredbhīma ekacitto vyavasthitaḥ .. 36 ..
1.206.d:
मार्तंडस्य इदं रूपं शुचिः स्नातो जितेंद्रियः॥
त्रिकालं यः स्मरेद्भीम एकचित्तो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 36 ॥
1.206.m: This is the form of Mārtaṇḍa. Pure, bathed, with senses restrained, / he who meditates on it at the three junctures of the day, established with a single mind, O Bhīma,

1.206.s:
so'cirādbhavate loke vittena dhanadopamaḥ ..
mucyate sarvabhogaistu tejasvī balavānbhavet .. 37 ..
1.206.d:
सोऽचिराद्भवते लोके वित्तेन धनदोपमः ॥
मुच्यते सर्वभोगैस्तु तेजस्वी बलवान्भवेत् ॥ 37 ॥
1.206.m: he soon becomes in the world equal to the giver of wealth [Kubera] in riches; / he is freed from all pleasures, and becomes splendid and strong.

1.206.s:
hṛdayaṃ cottamāṃgaṃ ca śikhā vai vaktrameva ca ..
raktavarṇā ime śyāmāḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ .. 38..
1.206.d:
हृदयं चोत्तमांगं च शिखा वै वक्त्रमेव च ॥
रक्तवर्णा इमे श्यामाः सर्वाभरणभूषिताः ॥ 38॥
1.206.m: The heart, the head, the crest, and the face— / these are red in colour or dark, adorned with all ornaments.

1.206.s:
varadā'bhayahastāśca dhyātavyā sādhakena tu ..
taḍitpuṃjanibhaṃ śastraṃ raudraṃ caṃdrakarālinam .. 39 ..
1.206.d:
वरदाऽभयहस्ताश्च ध्यातव्या साधकेन तु ॥
तडित्पुंजनिभं शस्त्रं रौद्रं चंद्रकरालिनम् ॥ 39 ॥
1.206.m: They are to be meditated upon by the practitioner with hands granting boons and fearlessness, / with a weapon resembling a mass of lightning, terrible, terrifying like the moon.

1.206.s:
viśeṣaḥ kathito hyeṣa kāmarūpaḥ svabhāvataḥ ..
dīptā dīptaśikhākārā dhyātavyā mama śaktayaḥ .. 40 ..
1.206.d:
विशेषः कथितो ह्येष कामरूपः स्वभावतः ॥
दीप्ता दीप्तशिखाकारा ध्यातव्या मम शक्तयः ॥ 40 ॥
1.206.m: This specific detail has been told, which assumes forms at will by its own nature. / Dīptā has the appearance of a flaming crest; my śaktis are to be meditated upon [thus].

1.206.s:
śvetavarṇaṃ smaretsomaṃ raktavarṇaṃ kujaṃ smaret ..
saumyamaṣṭāpadābhaṃ ca guruṃ ca pītavarṇakam .. .. 41 ..
1.206.d:
श्वेतवर्णं स्मरेत्सोमं रक्तवर्णं कुजं स्मरेत् ॥
सौम्यमष्टापदाभं च गुरुं च पीतवर्णकम् ॥ ॥ 41 ॥
1.206.m: One should meditate on Soma as white in colour, on Kuja as red in colour, / on Saumya as having the lustre of gold, and on Guru as yellow in colour,

1.206.s:
śaṃkhakṣīranibhaṃ śvetaṃ kāṇaṃ cāṃjanasaṃnibham ..
rajāvartanibhaṃ rāhuṃ dhūmraṃ ca vikacaṃ smaret .. 42 ..
1.206.d:
शंखक्षीरनिभं श्वेतं काणं चांजनसंनिभम् ॥
रजावर्तनिभं राहुं धूम्रं च विकचं स्मरेत् ॥ 42 ॥
1.206.m: on Śukra as white resembling a conch or milk, and on Śani as resembling collyrium; / on Rāhu as resembling lapis lazuli, and on Ketu as smoky and dishevelled.

1.206.s:
vāmahastau kaṭinyastau dakṣiṇau cābhayapradau ..
raktabhrūraktanetrāsya ardhakāyakṛtāṃjaliḥ .. 43 ..
1.206.d:
वामहस्तौ कटिन्यस्तौ दक्षिणौ चाभयप्रदौ ॥
रक्तभ्रूरक्तनेत्रास्य अर्धकायकृतांजलिः ॥ 43 ॥
1.206.m: Their left hands are placed on their hips, and their right hands grant fearlessness; / having red eyebrows, red eyes, and red faces, with the upper half of the body joining hands in reverence.

1.206.s:
iti bhānuṃ grahaiḥ sārdhaṃ ye dhyāyaṃti nṛpottama ..
labhaṃte te mahāsiddhimacirānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. .. 44 ..
1.206.d:
इति भानुं ग्रहैः सार्धं ये ध्यायंति नृपोत्तम ॥
लभंते ते महासिद्धिमचिरान्नात्र संशयः ॥ ॥ 44 ॥
1.206.m: Those who thus meditate on the Sun together with the planets, O best of kings, / attain great perfection before long; of this there is no doubt.

1.206.s:
tavākhyātamidaṃ vaktraṃ grahāṇāṃ bhīṣma kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
yacchrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyaṃte bhuvi mānavāḥ .. 45 ..
1.206.d:
तवाख्यातमिदं वक्त्रं ग्रहाणां भीष्म कृत्स्नशः ॥
यच्छ्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यंते भुवि मानवाः ॥ 45 ॥
1.206.m: This mouth of the planets has been declared to you in full, O Bhīṣma; / hearing which, human beings on earth are freed from all sins.

1.206.s:
anena vidhinā bhīṣma sadā devaṃ divākaram..
trikālaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā vīra śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 46 ..
1.206.d:
अनेन विधिना भीष्म सदा देवं दिवाकरम्॥
त्रिकालं पूजयेद्भक्त्या वीर श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥ 46 ॥
1.206.m: According to this rite, O Bhīṣma, a hero endowed with faith / should always worship the god Divākara with devotion at the three junctures of the day.

1.206.s:
itthaṃ pūjayamānastu sarvadevaṃ divākaram ..
brahmahatyāvinirmukto mahādevatvamāpnuyāt.. 47 ..
1.206.d:
इत्थं पूजयमानस्तु सर्वदेवं दिवाकरम् ॥
ब्रह्महत्याविनिर्मुक्तो महादेवत्वमाप्नुयात्॥ 47 ॥
1.206.m: Worshipping the god of all, Divākara, in this manner, / freed from the sin of killing a brahmin, he attains the state of Mahādeva.

1.206.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sauradharmeṣu sūryapūjāmāhātmyavarṇanṃ nāma ṣaḍuttaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 206 ..
ādityapūjāvidhivarṇanam
1.206.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे सौरधर्मेषु सूर्यपूजामाहात्म्यवर्णन्ं नाम षडुत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 206 ॥
आदित्यपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
1.206.m:
Thus ends the two hundred and sixth chapter, named "Description of the Greatness of the Worship of the Sun", in the Solar Duties of the Seventh Kalpa in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Rite of Worshipping Āditya.

1.207.s:
.. bhīṣma uvāca .. ..
aho devasya māhātmyaṃ bhāskarasya tvayoditam ..
pūjayaṃti sadā hyenaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivādayaḥ .. 1 ..
1.207.d:
॥ भीष्म उवाच ॥ ॥
अहो देवस्य माहात्म्यं भास्करस्य त्वयोदितम् ॥
पूजयंति सदा ह्येनं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादयः ॥ 1 ॥
1.207.m: Bhīṣma said: / Ah, the greatness of the god Bhāskara has been declared by you! / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the other gods always worship him.

1.207.s:
.. .. vyāsa uvāca .. ..
evametanna saṃdeho yathā vadasi bhārata ..
nāsti sūryasamo devo nāsti sūryasamā gatiḥ .. 2 ..
1.207.d:
॥ ॥ व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
एवमेतन्न संदेहो यथा वदसि भारत ॥
नास्ति सूर्यसमो देवो नास्ति सूर्यसमा गतिः ॥ 2 ॥
1.207.m: Vyāsa said: / It is so, there is no doubt, just as you say, O Bhārata; / there is no god equal to the Sun, there is no goal equal to the Sun.

1.207.s:
nāsti sūryasamaṃ brahma nāsti sūryasamaṃ hutam ..
nāsti sūryasamo dharmo nāsti sūryasamaṃ dhanam .. 3 ..
1.207.d:
नास्ति सूर्यसमं ब्रह्म नास्ति सूर्यसमं हुतम् ॥
नास्ति सूर्यसमो धर्मो नास्ति सूर्यसमं धनम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.207.m: There is no brahman equal to the Sun, there is no oblation equal to the Sun; / there is no dharma equal to the Sun, there is no wealth equal to the Sun.

1.207.s:
nāsti sūryādṛte kāmo nāsti sūryādṛte padam ..
nāsti sūryasamo baṃdhurnāsti sūryasamaḥ suhṛt .. 4 ..
1.207.d:
नास्ति सूर्यादृते कामो नास्ति सूर्यादृते पदम् ॥
नास्ति सूर्यसमो बंधुर्नास्ति सूर्यसमः सुहृत् ॥ 4 ॥
1.207.m: There is no desire without the Sun, there is no realm without the Sun; / there is no relative equal to the Sun, there is no friend equal to the Sun.

1.207.s:
nāsti sūryasamā mātā nāsti sūryasamo guruḥ ..
nāsti sūryasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na pavitraṃ tataḥ param .. 5 ..
1.207.d:
नास्ति सूर्यसमा माता नास्ति सूर्यसमो गुरुः ॥
नास्ति सूर्यसमं तीर्थं न पवित्रं ततः परम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.207.m: There is no mother equal to the Sun, there is no guru equal to the Sun; / there is no sacred bathing place equal to the Sun, nor is there anything more purifying than it.

1.207.s:
tamekaṃ daivataṃ vidyānnaivāpyarkaparāyaṇam ..
lokānāṃ devatānāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ cāpi bhārata .. 6 ..
1.207.d:
तमेकं दैवतं विद्यान्नैवाप्यर्कपरायणम् ॥
लोकानां देवतानां च पितॄणां चापि भारत ॥ 6 ॥
1.207.m: One should know him as the one deity; there is no other refuge than Arka / for the worlds, for the deities, and also for the ancestors, O Bhārata.

1.207.s:
tamarcaṃtaḥ stuvaṃtaśca prāpnuvaṃti parāṃ gatim..
te prapannāstu ye bhaktyā muktāste bhavasāgarāt.. 7 ..
1.207.d:
तमर्चंतः स्तुवंतश्च प्राप्नुवंति परां गतिम्॥
ते प्रपन्नास्तु ये भक्त्या मुक्तास्ते भवसागरात्॥ 7 ॥
1.207.m: Those who worship and praise him attain the supreme goal; / and those who take refuge in him with devotion are freed from the ocean of worldly existence.

1.207.s:
rājā corā grahāḥ sarpā dāridryaṃ duḥkhasaṃpadaḥ ..
naite pīḍayituṃ śaktāḥ prasanne bhāskare sati .. 8 ..
1.207.d:
राजा चोरा ग्रहाः सर्पा दारिद्र्यं दुःखसंपदः ॥
नैते पीडयितुं शक्ताः प्रसन्ने भास्करे सति ॥ 8 ॥
1.207.m: Kings, thieves, planets, serpents, poverty, and masses of sorrows— / these are not capable of afflicting anyone when Bhāskara is pleased.

1.207.s:
..vyāsa uvāca .. ..
evaṃ tāta mahābāho devo bhāskaratatparaḥ ..
sa pūjyaḥ sa namaskāryaḥ sa hi dhyātavya eva ca .. 9 ..
1.207.d:
॥व्यास उवाच ॥ ॥
एवं तात महाबाहो देवो भास्करतत्परः ॥
स पूज्यः स नमस्कार्यः स हि ध्यातव्य एव च ॥ 9 ॥
1.207.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus, O dear one, O mighty-armed one, the god is devoted to Bhāskara; / he is to be worshipped, he is to be bowed to, and he is indeed to be meditated upon.

1.207.s:
pratyakṣadevatā hyeṣā devadevoyamādarāt ..
atha kiṃ bahunoktena yadvakṣyāmi nibodha me .. 1.207.10 ..
1.207.d:
प्रत्यक्षदेवता ह्येषा देवदेवोयमादरात् ॥
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन यद्वक्ष्यामि निबोध मे ॥ 1.207.10 ॥
1.207.m: For this god of gods is a directly visible deity; with care / what is the use of speaking much? Listen to what I shall say to you.

1.207.s:
pūjayettanayaḥ pāpī tathādityadinairapi ..
pūjayanti narā ye vai te yāṃti paramāṃ gatim .. 11 ..
1.207.d:
पूजयेत्तनयः पापी तथादित्यदिनैरपि ॥
पूजयन्ति नरा ये वै ते यांति परमां गतिम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.207.m: Even a sinful son who worships on the days of the Sun— / those men who worship indeed go to the supreme goal.

1.207.s:
prāpte sūryadine bhaktyā bhānuṃ saṃpūjya śraddhayā ..
naktaṃ karoti puruṣaḥ sa yātyamaraloktām .. 12 ..
1.207.d:
प्राप्ते सूर्यदिने भक्त्या भानुं संपूज्य श्रद्धया ॥
नक्तं करोति पुरुषः स यात्यमरलोक्ताम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.207.m: When the day of the Sun has arrived, having worshipped Bhānu with devotion and with faith, / the man who eats a nocturnal meal goes to the realm of the immortals.

1.207.s:
yastu pūrvaṃ raverbhaktyā pañcaratnasamanvitam..
nivedayati maṃtreṇa sa yātyamaralokatām .. 13 ..
1.207.d:
यस्तु पूर्वं रवेर्भक्त्या पञ्चरत्नसमन्वितम्॥
निवेदयति मंत्रेण स यात्यमरलोकताम् ॥ 13 ॥
1.207.m: He who formerly, with devotion to Ravi, offers [an oblation] / endowed with the five jewels accompanied by the mantra, goes to the realm of the immortals.

1.207.s:
mārtaṃḍaprītaye yastu kuryācchrāddhaṃ vidhānataḥ ..
saṃkrāntāvayane vīra sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 14 ..
1.207.d:
मार्तंडप्रीतये यस्तु कुर्याच्छ्राद्धं विधानतः ॥
संक्रान्तावयने वीर सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 14 ॥
1.207.m: He who performs a śrāddha according to the rules for the satisfaction of Mārtaṇḍa / at a solstice or an equinox, O hero, goes to the realm of the Sun.

1.207.s:
kṛtvopavāsaṃ ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu saptamyāṃ yastu mānavaḥ ..
karoti vidhivacchrāddhaṃ bhāskaraḥ prīyatāmiti..15..
1.207.d:
कृत्वोपवासं षष्ठ्यां तु सप्तम्यां यस्तु मानवः ॥
करोति विधिवच्छ्राद्धं भास्करः प्रीयतामिति॥15॥
1.207.m: Having observed a fast on the sixth lunar day, that man who, on the seventh lunar day, / performs a śrāddha according to rule, saying: 'May Bhāskara be pleased!'

1.207.s:
sarvadoṣavinirmuktaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate ..
mānavo yastu saptamyāṃ yoṣidvāpi divākaram ..16..
1.207.d:
सर्वदोषविनिर्मुक्तः सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
मानवो यस्तु सप्तम्यां योषिद्वापि दिवाकरम् ॥16॥
1.207.m: freed from all faults, is glorified in the realm of the Sun. / The man or woman who, on the seventh lunar day, [worships] Divākara,

1.207.s:
prapūjya vidhivadbhānuṃ sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..
viśeṣatastasya dine grahaṇe ca narādhipa .. 17 ..
1.207.d:
प्रपूज्य विधिवद्भानुं सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
विशेषतस्तस्य दिने ग्रहणे च नराधिप ॥ 17 ॥
1.207.m: duly worshipping the Sun, shall obtain all desires, / especially on his day and at an eclipse, O lord of men.

1.207.s:
iti bhīṣma vijānīhi na devo bhāskarātpriyaḥ ..
ādityamekaṃ paramaṃ devadeveṣu pūjitam .. 18 ..
1.207.d:
इति भीष्म विजानीहि न देवो भास्करात्प्रियः ॥
आदित्यमेकं परमं देवदेवेषु पूजितम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.207.m: 'Know this, Bhīṣma: no deity is dearer than Bhāskara. / Āditya alone is supreme, worshipped among the gods of gods.

1.207.s:
ratnaparvatamāruhya yathā bhuvi narādhipāḥ ..
sattvānurūpaṃ gacchanti ratnabhāgānaśeṣataḥ .. 19 ..
1.207.d:
रत्नपर्वतमारुह्य यथा भुवि नराधिपाः ॥
सत्त्वानुरूपं गच्छन्ति रत्नभागानशेषतः ॥ 19 ॥
1.207.m: Just as lords of men on earth, having climbed a mountain of gems, / obtain shares of gems entirely in accordance with their strength,

1.207.s:
tathā bhānuṃ samārādhya prāpnuvaṃti narāḥ phalam..
dhanārthī prāpnuyādarthaṃ putrārthī prāpnuyātsutam .. 1.207.20 ..
1.207.d:
तथा भानुं समाराध्य प्राप्नुवंति नराः फलम्॥
धनार्थी प्राप्नुयादर्थं पुत्रार्थी प्राप्नुयात्सुतम् ॥ 1.207.20 ॥
1.207.m: so men, having propitiated the Sun, obtain reward: / one who desires wealth would obtain wealth; one who desires a son would obtain a son;

1.207.s:
mokṣārthī mokṣamāpnoti cātha vā'maratāṃ vrajet ..
atha kiṃ bahunoktena śṛṇu tvaṃ vacanaṃ mama .. 21 ..
1.207.d:
मोक्षार्थी मोक्षमाप्नोति चाथ वाऽमरतां व्रजेत् ॥
अथ किं बहुनोक्तेन शृणु त्वं वचनं मम ॥ 21 ॥
1.207.m: one who desires liberation attains liberation, or would go to the state of an immortal. / Now, what is the use of much talk? Hear my word:

1.207.s:
brahmādayo devagaṇā bhānumārādhya bhārata ..
manoharāṇi divyāni divi sthānānyavāpnuvan .. 22 ..
1.207.d:
ब्रह्मादयो देवगणा भानुमाराध्य भारत ॥
मनोहराणि दिव्यानि दिवि स्थानान्यवाप्नुवन् ॥ 22 ॥
1.207.m: The hosts of gods, headed by Brahmā, having propitiated the Sun, O Bhārata, / obtained charming, divine abodes in heaven,

1.207.s: acalāni mahābhāgāḥ sarvapāpaharāṇi ca .. 23 ..
1.207.d: अचलानि महाभागाः सर्वपापहराणि च ॥ 23 ॥
1.207.m: unshakeable, O fortunate one, and removing all sins.'

1.207.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
ityuktvā bhagavānvyāsastatraivāṃtaradhīyata ..
bhīṣmo'pi pūjayāmāsa bhaktyā bhānuṃ vidhānataḥ ..24..
1.207.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्व्यासस्तत्रैवांतरधीयत ॥
भीष्मोऽपि पूजयामास भक्त्या भानुं विधानतः ॥24॥
1.207.m: Sumantu said: / Having spoken thus, the venerable Vyāsa vanished right there. / Bhīṣma, too, worshipped the Sun with devotion according to rule.

1.207.s:
tathā tvamapi rājendra pūjayemaṃ divākaram ..
pūjayitvā raviṃ bhaktyā sthānaṃ yāsyasi śāśvatam ..25..
1.207.d:
तथा त्वमपि राजेन्द्र पूजयेमं दिवाकरम् ॥
पूजयित्वा रविं भक्त्या स्थानं यास्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥25॥
1.207.m: Likewise you also, O king of kings, worship this Divākara. / Having worshipped the Sun with devotion, you shall go to the eternal abode,

1.207.s:
yathā gataḥ sa bhagavānvyāso bhīṣmaśca mānada ..
sakṛtprapūjya saptamyāṃ bhaktyā devaṃ divākaram .. 26 ..
saptamīvratavarṇanam
1.207.d:
यथा गतः स भगवान्व्यासो भीष्मश्च मानद ॥
सकृत्प्रपूज्य सप्तम्यां भक्त्या देवं दिवाकरम् ॥ 26 ॥
सप्तमीव्रतवर्णनम्
1.207.m:
just as the venerable Vyāsa and Bhīṣma went, O giver of honor, / having worshipped God Divākara once with devotion on the seventh lunar day.
Description of the Saptamī Votive Observance

1.208.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
punarme brūhi saptamyāṃ prītaye bhāskarasya tu ..
upoṣito bhavatīha naro yastu dvijottama .. 1 ..
1.208.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
पुनर्मे ब्रूहि सप्तम्यां प्रीतये भास्करस्य तु ॥
उपोषितो भवतीह नरो यस्तु द्विजोत्तम ॥ 1 ॥
1.208.m: Śatānīka said: / Tell me again, O best of twice-borns, regarding the man here / who has fasted on the seventh lunar day for the pleasure of Bhāskara.

1.208.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
kathitāḥ sapta saptamyaḥ punarasminmahāmate ..
bahavaḥ kuruśārdūla bhūyastvetāḥ śṛṇuṣva me .. 2 ..
1.208.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
कथिताः सप्त सप्तम्यः पुनरस्मिन्महामते ॥
बहवः कुरुशार्दूल भूयस्त्वेताः शृणुष्व मे ॥ 2 ॥
1.208.m: Sumantu said: / Seven seventh lunar days were spoken of again in this [matter], O wise one; / they are many, O tiger of the Kurus. Listen further to these from me,

1.208.s:
svayaṃ yāḥ kathitāḥ pūrvamādityena khagādhipa ..
aruṇasya mahābāho saptamyaḥ sapta pūjitāḥ .. 3 ..
1.208.d:
स्वयं याः कथिताः पूर्वमादित्येन खगाधिप ॥
अरुणस्य महाबाहो सप्तम्यः सप्त पूजिताः ॥ 3 ॥
1.208.m: which were declared of old by Āditya himself to Aruṇa, O king of birds! / O strong-armed one, the revered seven seventh lunar days [are as follows]:

1.208.s:
arkasaṃpuṭakairekā dvitīyā maricaistathā ..
tṛtīyā niṃbapatraiśca caturthī phalasaptamī .. 4 ..
1.208.d:
अर्कसंपुटकैरेका द्वितीया मरिचैस्तथा ॥
तृतीया निंबपत्रैश्च चतुर्थी फलसप्तमी ॥ 4 ॥
1.208.m: One is with swallow-wort calyxes; the second with black peppercorns; / the third with neem leaves; the fourth is the Fruit-Seventh;

1.208.s:
anodanā pañcamī syātṣaṣṭhī vijayasaptamī ..
saptamī kāmikā jñeyā vidhiṃ tāsāṃ nibodha me .. 5 ..
1.208.d:
अनोदना पञ्चमी स्यात्षष्ठी विजयसप्तमी ॥
सप्तमी कामिका ज्ञेया विधिं तासां निबोध मे ॥ 5 ॥
1.208.m: the fifth is Non-grain; the sixth is Vijayasaptamī; / the seventh is to be known as Kāmikā. Learn their rule from me.

1.208.s:
śuklapakṣe ravidine dakṣiṇe cottarāyaṇe ..
grahaṇe sūryanakṣatre gṛhṇīyātsapta saptamī .. 6 ..
1.208.d:
शुक्लपक्षे रविदिने दक्षिणे चोत्तरायणे ॥
ग्रहणे सूर्यनक्षत्रे गृह्णीयात्सप्त सप्तमी ॥ 6 ॥
1.208.m: In the bright fortnight, on a Sunday, at the southern or northern solstice, / at an eclipse, or on a Sun-asterism, one should undertake the seven seventh lunar days.

1.208.s:
sa tāṃ su brahmacārī syācchaucayukto jitendriyaḥ ..
sūryārcanarato dāṃto japahomaparastathā .. 7 ..
1.208.d:
स तां सु ब्रह्मचारी स्याच्छौचयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
सूर्यार्चनरतो दांतो जपहोमपरस्तथा ॥ 7 ॥
1.208.m: During these, he should be celibate, pure, with senses conquered, / devoted to worshipping the Sun, subdued, and intent upon repetition and oblation.

1.208.s:
pañcamyāmeva puruṣaḥ kuryānnitya manātmakam ..
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ na maithunaṃ gacchenmadhumāṃsaṃ ca varjayet .. 8 ..
1.208.d:
पञ्चम्यामेव पुरुषः कुर्यान्नित्य मनात्मकम् ॥
षष्ठ्यां न मैथुनं गच्छेन्मधुमांसं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
1.208.m: On the fifth lunar day itself a man should perform his daily rite without self-indulgence; / on the sixth he should not engage in sexual intercourse and should avoid honey and meat.

1.208.s:
arkasaṃpuṭakairekāṃ tathānyāṃ maricairnayet ..
tathāparāṃ niṃbapatraiḥ phalākhyāyāṃ phalaṃ caret .. 9 ..
1.208.d:
अर्कसंपुटकैरेकां तथान्यां मरिचैर्नयेत् ॥
तथापरां निंबपत्रैः फलाख्यायां फलं चरेत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.208.m: One should pass one with swallow-wort calyxes, another with black peppercorns, / another with neem leaves; on that called Fruit, one should consume fruit.

1.208.s:
anodanāmannarahita upāsīta yathāvidhi ..
ahorātraṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ kuryādvijayasaptamīm .. 1.208.10 ..
1.208.d:
अनोदनामन्नरहित उपासीत यथाविधि ॥
अहोरात्रं वायुभक्षः कुर्याद्विजयसप्तमीम् ॥ 1.208.10 ॥
1.208.m: On Non-grain, destitute of grain, he should worship duly; / subsisting on air for a day and night, he should observe Vijayasaptamī.

1.208.s:
tathaikāṃ saptamīṃ kṛtvā pratimāsaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
kuryādyathāvidhi mudā tataḥ kurvīta kāmikām .. 11 ..
1.208.d:
तथैकां सप्तमीं कृत्वा प्रतिमासं विचक्षणः ॥
कुर्याद्यथाविधि मुदा ततः कुर्वीत कामिकाम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.208.m: Having thus observed one seventh lunar day month by month, the wise one / should perform [it] duly with joy; thereafter he should perform Kāmikā.

1.208.s:
āsāṃ likhitvā nāmāni patrakeṣu pṛthakpṛthak ..
tāni sarvāṇi patrāṇi kṣipedabhinave ghaṭe .. 12 ..
1.208.d:
आसां लिखित्वा नामानि पत्रकेषु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
तानि सर्वाणि पत्राणि क्षिपेदभिनवे घटे ॥ 12 ॥
1.208.m: Having written their names separately on leaves, / he should drop all those leaves into a new earthen pot.

1.208.s:
tadarthaṃ yo na jānāti lokavāhyopi vā naraḥ ..
tena hyuddhārayedekaṃ na kuryācca vicāraṇām ..13..
1.208.d:
तदर्थं यो न जानाति लोकवाह्योपि वा नरः ॥
तेन ह्युद्धारयेदेकं न कुर्याच्च विचारणाम् ॥13॥
1.208.m: A man who does not know their meaning, or even one excluded from people, / by him one [leaf] should be drawn out, and one should make no hesitation.

1.208.s:
tenaiva vidhinā yastu pratimāsaṃ ca tattapaḥ ..
saptaiva yāvatsaptamyo vijñeyā sā tu kāmikā .. 14 ..
1.208.d:
तेनैव विधिना यस्तु प्रतिमासं च तत्तपः ॥
सप्तैव यावत्सप्तम्यो विज्ञेया सा तु कामिका ॥ 14 ॥
1.208.m: By that very rule he who [performs] that asceticism month by month, / for as many as seven seventh lunar days—that is to be known as Kāmikā.

1.208.s:
ityetāḥ sapta saptamyaḥ svayaṃ proktā vivasvatā ..
kurvīta yo naro bhaktyā sa yātyarkasado nṛpa .. 15 ..
1.208.d:
इत्येताः सप्त सप्तम्यः स्वयं प्रोक्ता विवस्वता ॥
कुर्वीत यो नरो भक्त्या स यात्यर्कसदो नृप ॥ 15 ॥
1.208.m: Thus these seven seventh lunar days were declared by Vivasvat himself; / whatever man performs them with devotion, he goes to the Sun's abode, O king.

1.208.s:
arkasaṃpuṭakairvittamacalaṃ saptapauruṣam ..
maricaiḥ saṃgamaḥ syādvai priyaiḥ putrādibhiḥ sadā .. 16 ..
1.208.d:
अर्कसंपुटकैर्वित्तमचलं सप्तपौरुषम् ॥
मरिचैः संगमः स्याद्वै प्रियैः पुत्रादिभिः सदा ॥ 16 ॥
1.208.m: By swallow-wort calyxes comes unshakeable wealth enduring for seven generations; / by black peppercorns, there will indeed always be union with dear ones, such as sons;

1.208.s:
sarvarogāḥ praṇaśyaṃti niṃbapatrairna saṃśayaḥ ..
phalaistu putrapautrāśca dauhitraścāpi puṣkalaḥ .. 17 ..
1.208.d:
सर्वरोगाः प्रणश्यंति निंबपत्रैर्न संशयः ॥
फलैस्तु पुत्रपौत्राश्च दौहित्रश्चापि पुष्कलः ॥ 17 ॥
1.208.m: by neem leaves, all diseases are destroyed, no doubt; / by fruits, sons, grandsons, and abundant daughter's sons [are gained];

1.208.s:
ato dhanaṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā ..
tathā paśurhiraṇyaṃ ca ārogyaṃ satataṃ nṛpa .. 18 ..
1.208.d:
अतो धनं धनं धान्यं सुवर्णं रजतं तथा ॥
तथा पशुर्हिरण्यं च आरोग्यं सततं नृप ॥ 18 ॥
1.208.m: from this, wealth, grain, gold, and silver, / as well as cattle, wealth, and constant health, O king.

1.208.s:
upoṣya vijayāṃ śatrūnrājañjayati nityaśaḥ ..
sādhayetkāmadā kāmānvidhivatsamupāsitā .. 19 ..
1.208.d:
उपोष्य विजयां शत्रून्राजञ्जयति नित्यशः ॥
साधयेत्कामदा कामान्विधिवत्समुपासिता ॥ 19 ॥
1.208.m: Having fasted on Vijayā, he constantly conquers enemies, O king; / worshipped according to rule, the wish-granting [observance] accomplishes wishes.

1.208.s:
putrakāmo labhetputramarthakāmorthamakṣayam ..
vidyākāmo labhedvidyāṃ rājyārthī rājyamāpnuyāt ..
kṛtsnānkāmāndadātyeṣā kāmadā kurunandana .. 1.208.20 ..
1.208.d:
पुत्रकामो लभेत्पुत्रमर्थकामोर्थमक्षयम् ॥
विद्याकामो लभेद्विद्यां राज्यार्थी राज्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
कृत्स्नान्कामान्ददात्येषा कामदा कुरुनन्दन ॥ 1.208.20 ॥
1.208.m: He who desires a son obtains a son; he who desires wealth, imperishable wealth; / he who desires learning obtains learning; he who desires kingship obtains a kingdom. / It gives all desires, this wish-granting [observance], O joy of the Kurus.

1.208.s:
naro vā yadi vā nārī yathoktaṃ saptamīvratam ..
karoti niyatātmā vai sa yāti paramāṃ gatim .. 21 ..
1.208.d:
नरो वा यदि वा नारी यथोक्तं सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥
करोति नियतात्मा वै स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.208.m: Whether a man or a woman, self-restrained indeed, / performs the votive observance of the seventh lunar day as described, he goes to the supreme state.

1.208.s:
na teṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcidastīti durlabham ..
ye bhaktyā lokanāthasya vratinaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ .. 22 ..
1.208.d:
न तेषां त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचिदस्तीति दुर्लभम् ॥
ये भक्त्या लोकनाथस्य व्रतिनः संशितव्रताः ॥ 22 ॥
1.208.m: There is nothing difficult to attain for them in the three worlds / who are observers of the votive observance, firm in vows, through devotion to the lord of the world.

1.208.s:
vrataistu vividhairvīra tapobhirvā suduṣkaraiḥ ..
na tatphalamavāpnoti yajñairvā bahudakṣiṇaiḥ .. 23 ..
1.208.d:
व्रतैस्तु विविधैर्वीर तपोभिर्वा सुदुष्करैः ॥
न तत्फलमवाप्नोति यज्ञैर्वा बहुदक्षिणैः ॥ 23 ॥
1.208.m: That fruit is not obtained by various votive observances, O hero, or by austerities very difficult to perform, / or by sacrifices with lavish sacrificial fees,

1.208.s:
tīrthābhiṣecanairvāpi dānahomārcanaistathā ..
yatphalaṃ ca pūjayituṃ saptamyāṃ prāpya mokṣadam ..
mokṣārthī pārthivaśreṣṭha yathāha bhagavānraviḥ .. 24 ..
1.208.d:
तीर्थाभिषेचनैर्वापि दानहोमार्चनैस्तथा ॥
यत्फलं च पूजयितुं सप्तम्यां प्राप्य मोक्षदम् ॥
मोक्षार्थी पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ यथाह भगवान्रविः ॥ 24 ॥
1.208.m: or by sacred-bathings at holy fords, or by gifts, oblations, and worship, / which fruit granting liberation is obtained by worshipping on the seventh lunar day / by one seeking liberation, O best of earthly rulers, as the venerable Sun said.

1.208.s:
kṛtvādityadine naktaṃ bhaktyā saṃpūjayedravim ..
acalaṃ sthānamāpnoti mānavaḥ śraddhayānvitaḥ ..
sūryaloke ca niyataṃ tasya vāso na saṃśayaḥ .. 25 ..
1.208.d:
कृत्वादित्यदिने नक्तं भक्त्या संपूजयेद्रविम् ॥
अचलं स्थानमाप्नोति मानवः श्रद्धयान्वितः ॥
सूर्यलोके च नियतं तस्य वासो न संशयः ॥ 25 ॥
1.208.m: Having observed a nocturnal meal on Sunday, one should worship the Sun with devotion; / endowed with faith, a man attains an unshakeable station, / and his residence in the Sun's realm is assured, there is no doubt.

1.208.s:
yastu pūjayate bhaktyā saptamyāṃ bhāskaraṃ naraḥ ..
brahmeṃdrarudralokeṣu tasyāpratihatā gatiḥ ..26 ..
1.208.d:
यस्तु पूजयते भक्त्या सप्तम्यां भास्करं नरः ॥
ब्रह्मेंद्ररुद्रलोकेषु तस्याप्रतिहता गतिः ॥26 ॥
1.208.m: The man who worships Bhāskara with devotion on the seventh lunar day, / his course is unimpeded in the realms of Brahmā, Indra, and Rudra.

1.208.s:
nāṃdho na kuṣṭhī na klībo na vyaṃgo na ca nirdhanaḥ ..
kule tasya bhavedvīra yaścaretsaptamīvratam .. 27 ..
1.208.d:
नांधो न कुष्ठी न क्लीबो न व्यंगो न च निर्धनः ॥
कुले तस्य भवेद्वीर यश्चरेत्सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥ 27 ॥
1.208.m: Neither blind, nor leprous, nor impotent, nor deformed, nor impoverished / will there be in the lineage of him, O hero, who would perform the votive observance of the seventh lunar day.

1.208.s:
vidyārthī labhate vidyāṃ dhanārthī dhanamāpnuyāt ..
bhāryārthī rūpasaṃpannāṃ striyaṃ putrāṃśca bhārata .. 28 ..
1.208.d:
विद्यार्थी लभते विद्यां धनार्थी धनमाप्नुयात् ॥
भार्यार्थी रूपसंपन्नां स्त्रियं पुत्रांश्च भारत ॥ 28 ॥
1.208.m: One seeking learning obtains learning; one seeking wealth obtains wealth; / one seeking a wife obtains a beautiful woman and sons, O Bhārata.

1.208.s:
lobhātpramādānmohācca vratabhaṃgo yadā bhavet ..
tadā trirātraṃ nāśnīyātkuryādvā keśamuṃḍanam ...29..
1.208.d:
लोभात्प्रमादान्मोहाच्च व्रतभंगो यदा भवेत् ॥
तदा त्रिरात्रं नाश्नीयात्कुर्याद्वा केशमुंडनम् ॥.29॥
1.208.m: When a break in the votive observance occurs out of greed, negligence, or delusion, / then he should not eat for three nights, or should shave his hair.

1.208.s:
prāyaścittamidaṃ kṛtvā punareva vratī bhavet ..
saptaiva yāvatsaptamyo bhavaṃti ca khageśvara..1.208.30..
1.208.d:
प्रायश्चित्तमिदं कृत्वा पुनरेव व्रती भवेत् ॥
सप्तैव यावत्सप्तम्यो भवंति च खगेश्वर॥1.208.30॥
1.208.m: Having performed this expiation, one should again undertake the vrata / until just seven saptamīs have passed, O lord of birds.

1.208.s:
abhyarcya sūryasaptamyāṃ mālyadhūpādibhirnaraḥ ..
bhojayitvā dvijāñchaktyā prāpnuyātsvargamakṣayam..31..
1.208.d:
अभ्यर्च्य सूर्यसप्तम्यां माल्यधूपादिभिर्नरः ॥
भोजयित्वा द्विजाञ्छक्त्या प्राप्नुयात्स्वर्गमक्षयम्॥31॥
1.208.m: Having worshipped on Sūryasaptamī with garlands, incense, and other offerings, / and having fed Brahmins according to one's means, a man attains imperishable heaven.

1.208.s:
saptamyāṃ vipramukhyebhyo hiraṇyaṃ yaḥ prayacchati..
sa tadakṣayyamāpnoti sūryalokaṃ ca gacchati ..32..
1.208.d:
सप्तम्यां विप्रमुख्येभ्यो हिरण्यं यः प्रयच्छति॥
स तदक्षय्यमाप्नोति सूर्यलोकं च गच्छति ॥32॥
1.208.m: He who bestows gold upon the foremost Brahmins on the saptamī / attains that imperishable reward and goes to the world of the sun.

1.208.s:
itīdaṃ kīrtitaṃ vīra saptamīvratamuttamam..
bhūya evābhidhāsyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanā nṛpa ..33..
saptamīvratavarṇanam
1.208.d:
इतीदं कीर्तितं वीर सप्तमीव्रतमुत्तमम्॥
भूय एवाभिधास्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप ॥33॥
सप्तमीव्रतवर्णनम्
1.208.m:
Thus has this supreme saptamī-vrata been proclaimed, O hero. / I shall speak yet again; listen with a focused mind, O king.
Description of the Saptamī-Vrata

1.209.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
yaḥ kṣipedgomayāhāraḥ śuklā dvādaśa saptamīḥ ..
athavā yāvakāhāraḥ śīrṇaparṇāśano'pi vā .. 1 ..
1.209.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
यः क्षिपेद्गोमयाहारः शुक्ला द्वादश सप्तमीः ॥
अथवा यावकाहारः शीर्णपर्णाशनोऽपि वा ॥ 1 ॥
1.209.m: Sumantu said: / He who spends twelve bright saptamīs subsisting on cow dung, / or subsisting on barley gruel, or eating fallen leaves,

1.209.s:
kṣīrāśī caikabhakto vā bhikṣāhārotha vā punaḥ ..
jalāhāropi vā vidvānpūjayitvā divākaram .. 2 ..
1.209.d:
क्षीराशी चैकभक्तो वा भिक्षाहारोथ वा पुनः ॥
जलाहारोपि वा विद्वान्पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.209.m: or consuming milk, or eating once a day, or living on begged food, / or subsisting on water, having worshipped the maker of day, the wise man,
with diverse floral offerings—lotuses, saugandhika lilies, and water-lilies— / and with various kinds of perfumes, and incenses of guggulu and sandalwood,
with black perfume, milk-rice, and the like, and splendid ornaments, / and having worshipped the best of Brahmins with gold, food, and other gifts, a man

1.209.s:
sa tatphalamavāpnoti kratubhirbhūridakṣiṇaiḥ ..
yadeha tapyate vīra prāpyate kevalaṃ raveḥ .. 5
1.209.d:
स तत्फलमवाप्नोति क्रतुभिर्भूरिदक्षिणैः ॥
यदेह तप्यते वीर प्राप्यते केवलं रवेः ॥ 5
1.209.m: attains that reward which is gained through sacrifices with abundant sacrificial gifts. / What is endured here in austerity, O hero, is obtained solely from the sun.

1.209.s:
vimānavaramārūḍhaḥ sūryaloke mahīyate ..
tataḥ puṇyakṣayādrājankule mahati jāyate .. 6 ..
1.209.d:
विमानवरमारूढः सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
ततः पुण्यक्षयाद्राजन्कुले महति जायते ॥ 6 ॥
1.209.m: Mounted on an excellent celestial chariot, he is glorified in the world of the sun. / Then, when his merit is exhausted, O king, he is born into a great lineage.

1.209.s:
evaṃ bhaktyā vivasvaṃtaṃ pratimāsaṃ samāhitaḥ ..
pūjayedvidhivadbhaktyā nāmāni parikīrtayet .. 7 ..
1.209.d:
एवं भक्त्या विवस्वंतं प्रतिमासं समाहितः ॥
पूजयेद्विधिवद्भक्त्या नामानि परिकीर्तयेत् ॥ 7 ॥
1.209.m: In this manner, composed with devotion, every month / he should worship Vivasvat according to the rules and, with devotion, recite his names:

1.209.s:
caitrike māsi viṣṇuśca mādhave hyaryameti vai ..
śukre vivasvā nmāse tu śucau māse divākaraḥ .. 8 ..
1.209.d:
चैत्रिके मासि विष्णुश्च माधवे ह्यर्यमेति वै ॥
शुक्रे विवस्वा न्मासे तु शुचौ मासे दिवाकरः ॥ 8 ॥
1.209.m: In the month of Caitra, Viṣṇu; and in Mādhava, Aryaman; / in the month of Śukra, Vivasvat; and in the month of Śuci, Divākara;

1.209.s:
parjanyaḥ śrāvaṇe māsi nabhasye varuṇastathā ..
mārtaṃḍeti ca vijñeyaḥ kārtike bhārgavaḥ punaḥ .. 9 ..
1.209.d:
पर्जन्यः श्रावणे मासि नभस्ये वरुणस्तथा ॥
मार्तंडेति च विज्ञेयः कार्तिके भार्गवः पुनः ॥ 9 ॥
1.209.m: Parjanya in the month of Śrāvaṇa; and in Nabhasya, Varuṇa; / he should be known as Mārtaṇḍa [in Āśvina], and again as Bhārgava in Kārtika;

1.209.s:
mārgaśīrṣepi mitrastu kīrtitaḥ satataṃ budhaiḥ ..
pūṣā pauṣe tu vai māse pūjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ .. 10 ..
1.209.d:
मार्गशीर्षेपि मित्रस्तु कीर्तितः सततं बुधैः ॥
पूषा पौषे तु वै मासे पूजनीयः प्रयत्नतः ॥ 10 ॥
1.209.m: and in Mārgaśīrṣa, Mitra is ever proclaimed by the wise; / Pūṣan is to be worshipped with effort in the month of Pauṣa;

1.209.s:
māghe bhageti vijñeyastvaṣṭā caivātha phālgune ..
evaṃ krameṇa nāmāni kīrtayetprītaye raveḥ .. 11 ..
1.209.d:
माघे भगेति विज्ञेयस्त्वष्टा चैवाथ फाल्गुने ॥
एवं क्रमेण नामानि कीर्तयेत्प्रीतये रवेः ॥ 11 ॥
1.209.m: in Māgha he is to be known as Bhaga, and Tvaṣṭṛ in Phālguna. / Thus in order he should recite the names for the pleasure of the sun.

1.209.s:
dhūpārcanavidhimimaṃ saptamyāṃ susamāhitaḥ ..
yaḥ karoti naro bhaktyā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim .. 12 ..
1.209.d:
धूपार्चनविधिमिमं सप्तम्यां सुसमाहितः ॥
यः करोति नरो भक्त्या स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.209.m: A man who, well-composed, performs this rite of incense and worship / on the saptamī with devotion goes to the supreme state.

1.209.s:
tataste sarvamākhyātaṃ yathāguhyatamaṃ vibhoḥ ..
naiva deyamaśiṣyāya nābhaktāya kadācana ..13..
1.209.d:
ततस्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यथागुह्यतमं विभोः ॥
नैव देयमशिष्याय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ॥13॥
1.209.m: Thus everything has been told to you as the deepest secret of the Lord. / It should never be given to one who is not a disciple, nor to one who lacks devotion,

1.209.s:
na ca pāpakṛte deyaṃ na deyaṃ nāstikāya vā..
kṛtaghne nāstike vīra na deyaṃ krūrakarmaṇi .. 14 ..
1.209.d:
न च पापकृते देयं न देयं नास्तिकाय वा॥
कृतघ्ने नास्तिके वीर न देयं क्रूरकर्मणि ॥ 14 ॥
1.209.m: nor should it be given to an evildoer, nor should it be given to an atheist, / to an ungrateful person, to an unbeliever, O hero, nor to one of cruel deeds.

1.209.s:
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyānnityaṃ saptamīvratamuttamam ..
paṭhedyaścāpi niyataḥ śraddhayā parayānvitaḥ .. 15 ..
1.209.d:
य इदं शृणुयान्नित्यं सप्तमीव्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
पठेद्यश्चापि नियतः श्रद्धया परयान्वितः ॥ 15 ॥
1.209.m: He who constantly listens to this supreme saptamī-vrata, / and he who, self-restrained, recites it endowed with supreme faith,

1.209.s:
iha loke sukhaṃ prāpya sūryaloke mahīyate ..
puṇyakṣayādihāgatya rājā bhavati bhūtale .. 16 .. ..
sūryapūjāvarṇanam
1.209.d:
इह लोके सुखं प्राप्य सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥
पुण्यक्षयादिहागत्य राजा भवति भूतले ॥ 16 ॥ ॥
सूर्यपूजावर्णनम्
1.209.m:
attains happiness in this world and is glorified in the world of the sun. / Returning here when his merit is exhausted, he becomes a king upon the earth.
Description of the Worship of Sūrya

1.210.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
ityeṣa saptamīkalpaḥ samāsātkathitastava..
vistarātte punarvacmi śṛṇu caikamanā vibho .. 1 ..
1.210.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
इत्येष सप्तमीकल्पः समासात्कथितस्तव॥
विस्तरात्ते पुनर्वच्मि शृणु चैकमना विभो ॥ 1 ॥
1.210.m: Sumantu said: / Thus this Saptamīkalpa has been told to you in brief. / I shall speak to you again in detail; listen with a focused mind, O lord.

1.210.s:
phālgunāmalapakṣasya ṣaṣṭhyāṃ ca samupoṣitaḥ ..
pūjayedbhāskaraṃ snātvā gaṃdhapuṣpavilepanaiḥ ..2..
1.210.d:
फाल्गुनामलपक्षस्य षष्ठ्यां च समुपोषितः ॥
पूजयेद्भास्करं स्नात्वा गंधपुष्पविलेपनैः ॥2॥
1.210.m: Having fasted on the sixth [lunar day] of the spotless fortnight of Phālguna, / one should bathe and worship Bhāskara with perfumes, flowers, and unguents,

1.210.s:
arkapuṣpairmahābāho guggulena sugaṃdhinā ..
śvetena karavīreṇa caṃdanena divākaram ..3.
1.210.d:
अर्कपुष्पैर्महाबाहो गुग्गुलेन सुगंधिना ॥
श्वेतेन करवीरेण चंदनेन दिवाकरम् ॥3.
1.210.m: with arka flowers, O mighty-armed one, with fragrant guggulu, / with white oleander, and with sandalwood—the maker of day.

1.210.s:
guḍodakena naivedyaṃ nivedyaṃ prītaye raveḥ ..
evaṃ pūjya divā bhānuṃ rātrau tasyāgrataḥ svapet..
japanbhaumaṃ paraṃ jāpyaṃ vinidraḥ satataṃ budhaḥ..4
1.210.d:
गुडोदकेन नैवेद्यं निवेद्यं प्रीतये रवेः ॥
एवं पूज्य दिवा भानुं रात्रौ तस्याग्रतः स्वपेत्॥
जपन्भौमं परं जाप्यं विनिद्रः सततं बुधः॥4
1.210.m: An offering of jaggery-water should be presented for the pleasure of the sun. / Having thus worshipped Bhānu by day, one should sleep at night before him, / continuously sleepless, wise, muttering the supreme earthly prayer.

1.210.s:
śatānīka uvāca
kiṃ tatparaṃ bhagavataḥ priyaṃ jāpyamanuttamam . . 5
1.210.d:
शतानीक उवाच
किं तत्परं भगवतः प्रियं जाप्यमनुत्तमम् ॥ 5
1.210.m: Śatānīka said: / What is that supreme, peerless prayer dear to the Lord,

1.210.s:
japtavyo yatparairbhaktyā bhānustasyāgrato naraiḥ .
tanme brūhi tathā mantrāndhūpadīpānviśeṣataḥ . .
yenāhaṃ taṃ japañjapyaṃ pūjayāmi divākaram . . 6
1.210.d:
जप्तव्यो यत्परैर्भक्त्या भानुस्तस्याग्रतो नरैः ।
तन्मे ब्रूहि तथा मन्त्रान्धूपदीपान्विशेषतः ॥
येनाहं तं जपञ्जप्यं पूजयामि दिवाकरम् ॥ 6
1.210.m: which should be muttered with devotion by men devoted to him, before Bhānu? / Tell me that, and especially the mantras, the incenses, and the lamps, / by which I, muttering that prayer, may worship the maker of day.

1.210.s:
sumanturuvāca
vacmi te bharataśreṣṭha samāsānna tu vistarāt . . 7
1.210.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
वच्मि ते भरतश्रेष्ठ समासान्न तु विस्तरात् ॥ 7
1.210.m: Sumantu said: / I shall tell you, O best of the Bharatas, in brief and not at length.

1.210.s:
ṣaḍakṣareṇa mantreṇa kuryātsarvaṃ samāhitaḥ .
japaṃ homaṃ tathā pūjāṃ śatajaptena sarvadā . . 8
1.210.d:
षडक्षरेण मन्त्रेण कुर्यात्सर्वं समाहितः ।
जपं होमं तथा पूजां शतजप्तेन सर्वदा ॥ 8
1.210.m: Composed, one should perform everything with the six-syllable mantra— / the recitation, the fire offering, and the worship—ever with [a mantra] recited a hundred times.

1.210.s:
sāvitryā ca japaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtvā śatasahasraśaḥ .
paścātsarvaṃ prakurvīta japādikamanākulam . . 9
1.210.d:
सावित्र्या च जपं पूर्वं कृत्वा शतसहस्रशः ।
पश्चात्सर्वं प्रकुर्वीत जपादिकमनाकुलम् ॥ 9
1.210.m: Having first performed the recitation with the Sāvitrī [mantra] hundreds and thousands of times, / one should afterwards perform everything—the recitation and the rest—without agitation:

1.210.s:
oṃ bhoḥ sāvitri bhāskarāya sahasraraśmi dhīmahi .
tena sūryaḥ pracodayāt . . 1.210.10
1.210.d:
ओं भोः सावित्रि भास्कराय सहस्ररश्मि धीमहि ।
तेन सूर्यः प्रचोदयात् ॥ 1.210.10
1.210.m: "Oṃ. Hail, O Sāvitrī! We meditate upon Bhāskara, the thousand-rayed; / may Sūrya impel us through that."

1.210.s:
japa eva paraḥ proktaḥ saptamyāṃ bhānunā svayam .
japtvā sakṛdbhavetpūto mānavo nātra saṃśayaḥ . . 11
1.210.d:
जप एव परः प्रोक्तः सप्तम्यां भानुना स्वयम् ।
जप्त्वा सकृद्भवेत्पूतो मानवो नात्र संशयः ॥ 11
1.210.m: Recitation alone was proclaimed as supreme on the saptamī by Bhānu himself. / Having muttered it once, a mortal becomes purified; there is no doubt of this.

1.210.s:
prabhāte tvatha saptamyāṃ japanniyatamānasaḥ .
pūjayedbhānkaraṃ bhaktyā pūrvoktavidhinā nṛpa . . 12
1.210.d:
प्रभाते त्वथ सप्तम्यां जपन्नियतमानसः ।
पूजयेद्भान्करं भक्त्या पूर्वोक्तविधिना नृप ॥ 12
1.210.m: Then at dawn on the saptamī, muttering with a restrained mind, / one should worship Bhāskara with devotion according to the previously stated rule, O king,

1.210.s:
śraddhayā bhojayeccāpi brāhmaṇāñchaktito nṛpa .
divyānbhogāṃśca vidhivadbhakṣyabhojyairanekaśaḥ . . 13
1.210.d:
श्रद्धया भोजयेच्चापि ब्राह्मणाञ्छक्तितो नृप ।
दिव्यान्भोगांश्च विधिवद्भक्ष्यभोज्यैरनेकशः ॥ 13
1.210.m: and with faith feed Brahmins according to one's ability, O king, / with celestial pleasures duly, with diverse foods to chew and eat.

1.210.s:
vittaśāṭhyaṃ na kurvīta bhojakāṃśca prabhojayet .
na bhojayettathā'saurānsaurānyatnena bhojayet . . 14
1.210.d:
वित्तशाठ्यं न कुर्वीत भोजकांश्च प्रभोजयेत् ।
न भोजयेत्तथाऽसौरान्सौरान्यत्नेन भोजयेत् ॥ 14
1.210.m: One must not practice deceit with one's wealth, and one should feed the Bhojakas. / One should not feed non-Sauras; one should diligently feed the Sauras.

1.210.s:
śatānīka uvāca
ke bhojyā ke na vā bhojyā brāhmaṇā brahmavittama .
keṣu citteṣu saptamyāṃ devadevo divākaraḥ . . 15
1.210.d:
शतानीक उवाच
के भोज्या के न वा भोज्या ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवित्तम ।
केषु चित्तेषु सप्तम्यां देवदेवो दिवाकरः ॥ 15
1.210.m: Śatānīka said: / Who are to be fed and who are not to be fed among Brahmins, O best knower of Brahman? / In which minds does the god of gods, the maker of day, dwell on the saptamī?

1.210.s:
ghaṭībhojyo bhavedvipraḥ saptamīṃ kurute ca yaḥ .
saurabhinneṣvabhojyo yo yaśca bhukto divākare . . 16
1.210.d:
घटीभोज्यो भवेद्विप्रः सप्तमीं कुरुते च यः ।
सौरभिन्नेष्वभोज्यो यो यश्च भुक्तो दिवाकरे ॥ 16
1.210.m: A Brahmin who performs the saptamī is one who should be fed for an hour; / one who is not a Saura is not to be fed, nor one who has already eaten while the sun was up.

1.210.s:
ete bhojyā dvijā rājannādityena samāsataḥ .
proktāḥ kurukulaśreṣṭha tathā'bhojyāñchṛṇuṣva vai . . 17
1.210.d:
एते भोज्या द्विजा राजन्नादित्येन समासतः ।
प्रोक्ताः कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ तथाऽभोज्याञ्छृणुष्व वै ॥ 17
1.210.m: These Brahmins, O king, were declared in brief by Āditya as those to be fed, / O best of the Kuru lineage; now hear of those who are not to be fed:

1.210.s:
sabhāryaḥ sapatiryastu kuṣṭharogairhataśca yaḥ .
yaścānyadevatābhaktastathā nakṣatrasūcakaḥ . . 18
1.210.d:
सभार्यः सपतिर्यस्तु कुष्ठरोगैर्हतश्च यः ।
यश्चान्यदेवताभक्तस्तथा नक्षत्रसूचकः ॥ 18
1.210.m: One who is [erroneously] with a wife or with a husband, one afflicted with leprosy, / one who is devoted to another deity, and an astrologer;

1.210.s:
parāpavādanirato yaśca devalakastathā .
ete'bhojyāḥ savitrā tu svayaṃ devena cintitāḥ . . 19
1.210.d:
परापवादनिरतो यश्च देवलकस्तथा ।
एतेऽभोज्याः सवित्रा तु स्वयं देवेन चिन्तिताः ॥ 19
1.210.m: one intent on slandering others, and likewise a temple priest— / these have been considered by the god Savitṛ himself as unfit to be fed.

1.210.s:
śatānīka uvāca
ye bhojyā brāhmaṇāḥ proktā ye cābhojyā dvijottamāḥ .
eteṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ brūhi sarveṣāṃ vai samāhitaḥ . . 1.210.20
1.210.d:
शतानीक उवाच
ये भोज्या ब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्ता ये चाभोज्या द्विजोत्तमाः ।
एतेषां लक्षणं ब्रूहि सर्वेषां वै समाहितः ॥ 1.210.20
1.210.m: Śatānīka said: / As to those Brahmins who have been declared fit to be fed, and those best of Brahmins unfit to be fed, / tell me with a focused mind the characteristics of them all.

1.210.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭho'smi rājendra kīrtayāmyeva kṛtsnaśaḥ .
paṭhatāṃ tu trayī vidyāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ kadambakaḥ . . 21
1.210.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्ठोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र कीर्तयाम्येव कृत्स्नशः ।
पठतां तु त्रयी विद्यां ब्राह्मणानां कदम्बकः ॥ 21
1.210.m: Sumantu said: / I have been well asked, O lord of kings; I shall recount it in full. / Of Brahmins reciting the triple knowledge, a multitude...

1.210.s:
ghaṭetyuktā tu sā rājansvayaṃ devena bhānunā .
sā ghaṭā vidyate yasya sa ghaṭītyucyate dvijaiḥ . . 22
1.210.d:
घटेत्युक्ता तु सा राजन्स्वयं देवेन भानुना ।
सा घटा विद्यते यस्य स घटीत्युच्यते द्विजैः ॥ 22
1.210.m:
That, O king, was called a ghaṭā by the sun-god himself;
one who possesses such a ghaṭā is called a ghaṭin by the twice-born.

1.210.s:
brahmakṣatraviśāṃ vīra śūdrāṇāṃ ca kadambakaḥ .
śṛṇvatāṃ vidhivatpuṇyaṃ bhaktyā pustakavācanam . . 23
1.210.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रविशां वीर शूद्राणां च कदम्बकः ।
शृण्वतां विधिवत्पुण्यं भक्त्या पुस्तकवाचनम् ॥ 23
1.210.m:
An assembly of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, O hero, and of Śūdras,
who duly and with devotion listen to the recitation of the sacred book,

1.210.s:
iti māse nibaddhasya homasyeti ca bhānunā .
kathitaṃ kuruśārdūla svayamākāśagāminā . . 24
1.210.d:
इति मासे निबद्धस्य होमस्येति च भानुना ।
कथितं कुरुशार्दूल स्वयमाकाशगामिना ॥ 24
1.210.m:
of the fire offering that is tied to this month—thus, O tiger of the Kurus,
was it spoken by the sun himself, who traverses the sky.

1.210.s:
yasyāḥ kartā bhavedyastu mama syātkarako mataḥ .
sa vipro rājaśārdūla sadeṣṭo bhāskarasya tu . . 25
1.210.d:
यस्याः कर्ता भवेद्यस्तु मम स्यात्करको मतः ।
स विप्रो राजशार्दूल सदेष्टो भास्करस्य तु ॥ 25
1.210.m:
He who brings it about is regarded as my maker [of worship];
that Brahmin, O tiger among kings, is always dear to Bhāskara.

1.210.s:
jayopajīvī vyāsaśca samaḥ syājjīvakastathā .
yānyetāni purāṇāni setihāsāni bhārata . .
jayeti kathitānīha svayaṃ devena bhāsvatā . . 26
1.210.d:
जयोपजीवी व्यासश्च समः स्याज्जीवकस्तथा ।
यान्येतानि पुराणानि सेतिहासानि भारत ॥
जयेति कथितानीह स्वयं देवेन भास्वता ॥ 26
1.210.m:
One who lives by the Jaya [epic] and a Vyāsa are equal, as is a reciter.
Those Purāṇas along with the Itihāsas, O Bhārata,
are proclaimed here as ‘Jaya’ by the radiant god himself.

1.210.s:
ekaṃ nivāsayanyastu brāhmaṇaṃ tūpajīvati .
jayopajīvī sa jñeyo vācakaśca tathā nṛpa . . 27
1.210.d:
एकं निवासयन्यस्तु ब्राह्मणं तूपजीवति ।
जयोपजीवी स ज्ञेयो वाचकश्च तथा नृप ॥ 27
1.210.m:
One who, providing shelter to a single Brahmin, lives [by reciting it],
he is to be known as a ‘liver by the Jaya’ and as a reciter, O king.

1.210.s:
āruṇeyādiśāstrāṇi saptāśvatilakaṃ tathā .
yaśca jānāti saurāṇi vipraḥ saurassa tattvavit . . 28
1.210.d:
आरुणेयादिशास्त्राणि सप्ताश्वतिलकं तथा ।
यश्च जानाति सौराणि विप्रः सौरस्स तत्त्ववित् ॥ 28
1.210.m:
The Brahmin who knows the treatises beginning with Āruṇeya, the Saptāśvatilaka,
and the solar texts, is a Saura, one who knows reality.

1.210.s:
pūjayetsatataṃ yastu bhāskaraṃ nṛpasattama .
bhojakāṃśca tathā rājanyathā devaṃ divākaram . . 29
1.210.d:
पूजयेत्सततं यस्तु भास्करं नृपसत्तम ।
भोजकांश्च तथा राजन्यथा देवं दिवाकरम् ॥ 29
1.210.m:
He who continually worships Bhāskara, O best of kings,
and likewise the Bhojakas, O king, just as [he worships] the god who makes the day—

1.210.s:
sa jñeyo bhāskare bhakto bhojanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ ..
bhojyānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ hyetadabhojyānāṃ śṛṇuṣva me .. 1.210.30 ..
1.210.d:
स ज्ञेयो भास्करे भक्तो भोजनीयः प्रयत्नतः ॥
भोज्यानां लक्षणं ह्येतदभोज्यानां शृणुष्व मे ॥ 1.210.30 ॥
1.210.m:
he is to be recognized as devoted to Bhāskara and should be fed with care.
This is the mark of those fit to be fed; now hear from me of those who are not fit to be fed:

1.210.s:
vṛṣalī yasya vai bhāryā brāhmaṇasya viśeṣataḥ ..
parabhāryāpatirasau brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇādhamaḥ .. 31 ..
1.210.d:
वृषली यस्य वै भार्या ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः ॥
परभार्यापतिरसौ ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणाधमः ॥ 31 ॥
1.210.m:
A Brahmin whose wife is a Śūdra woman, in particular,
and one who takes another's wife—such a Brahmin is the vilest of Brahmins.

1.210.s:
daivena nihataḥ kuṣṭhī brāhmaṇo brahmaghātakaḥ ..
bhojako viṃdate yastu na ca taṃ pūjaye ttathā .. 32 ..
1.210.d:
दैवेन निहतः कुष्ठी ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मघातकः ॥
भोजको विंदते यस्तु न च तं पूजये त्तथा ॥ 32 ॥
1.210.m:
Struck by fate, a leper, a Brahmin who is a killer of a Brahmin,
or one who finds a Bhojaka and yet does not worship him in that manner—

1.210.s:
jñeyonyadevabhaktosau sa vipraḥ kurunaṃdana ..
ādityaṃ bhojakaṃ vidyādbhānordehasamudbhavam .. 33 ..
1.210.d:
ज्ञेयोन्यदेवभक्तोसौ स विप्रः कुरुनंदन ॥
आदित्यं भोजकं विद्याद्भानोर्देहसमुद्भवम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.210.m:
that Brahmin, O joy of the Kurus, is to be known as devoted to other gods.
One should know the Bhojaka to be Āditya, arisen from the body of the sun.

1.210.s:
nādityaṃ pūjayedyastu sa bhojyo na kadācana ..
muṇḍo vyaṃgadharo gauraḥ śaṃkhapuṣpadharastathā ..34..
1.210.d:
नादित्यं पूजयेद्यस्तु स भोज्यो न कदाचन ॥
मुण्डो व्यंगधरो गौरः शंखपुष्पधरस्तथा ॥34॥
1.210.m:
He who does not worship Āditya should never be fed;
likewise one who is shaven-headed, deformed, pale-skinned, or wearing conch-flower marks.

1.210.s:
yasya yāti gṛhe rājanbhojako mānavasya tu ..
tasya yāṃti gṛhe devāḥ pitaro bhāraka rasya tu .. 35 ..
1.210.d:
यस्य याति गृहे राजन्भोजको मानवस्य तु ॥
तस्य यांति गृहे देवाः पितरो भारक रस्य तु ॥ 35 ॥
1.210.m:
To the house of that man, O king, to which a Bhojaka goes,
the gods and the ancestors go, [as do those] of Bhāskara.

1.210.s:
rakṣobhūtapiśācāśca yoginyopi palāyitāḥ ..
sakṛdbhuṅkte gṛhe yasya bhojako gṛhadharmiṇaḥ .. 36 ..
1.210.d:
रक्षोभूतपिशाचाश्च योगिन्योपि पलायिताः ॥
सकृद्भुङ्क्ते गृहे यस्य भोजको गृहधर्मिणः ॥ 36 ॥
1.210.m:
Rākṣasas, ghosts, piśācas, and even yoginīs flee away.
In the house of whatever householder a Bhojaka eats even once,

1.210.s:
saptasaṃvatsaraṃ yāvatṛpto bhavati bhāskaraḥ ..
tasmāttānbhojayeddivyānbhojakānsatataṃ budhaḥ ..
yastu tānniṃdate vipraḥ sa na bhojyaḥ kadācana .. 37 ..
1.210.d:
सप्तसंवत्सरं यावतृप्तो भवति भास्करः ॥
तस्मात्तान्भोजयेद्दिव्यान्भोजकान्सततं बुधः ॥
यस्तु तान्निंदते विप्रः स न भोज्यः कदाचन ॥ 37 ॥
1.210.m:
Bhāskara remains satisfied for seven years.
Therefore, the wise man should continually feed those divine Bhojakas.
Any Brahmin who reviles them should never be fed.

1.210.s:
nijaṃ bhartāramutsṛjya svairaṃ yānyatra gacchati ..
svairiṇī sā tu vai proktā pāpiṣṭhā kuladūṣiṇī .. 38 ..
1.210.d:
निजं भर्तारमुत्सृज्य स्वैरं यान्यत्र गच्छति ॥
स्वैरिणी सा तु वै प्रोक्ता पापिष्ठा कुलदूषिणी ॥ 38 ॥
1.210.m:
A woman who abandons her own husband and goes elsewhere at her own whim
is called an unchaste woman (svairiṇī), most sinful, a defiler of her family.

1.210.s:
pracchannaṃ rocate rājanyā nārī bhavadoṣataḥ ..
jñeyā sā svairiṇī rājankule bhavati nāśinī ..39..
1.210.d:
प्रच्छन्नं रोचते राजन्या नारी भवदोषतः ॥
ज्ञेया सा स्वैरिणी राजन्कुले भवति नाशिनी ॥39॥
1.210.m:
A woman who, O king, delights in secret [amours] because of the fault of mundane passion,
is to be known as an unchaste woman, O king; she brings ruin upon her family.

1.210.s:
yo'syāṃ rato bhavedvipraḥ sa jñeyaḥ svairiṇīrataḥ ..
raṃgopajīvī kathako yaśca prākṛtanartakaḥ .. 1.210.40 ..
1.210.d:
योऽस्यां रतो भवेद्विप्रः स ज्ञेयः स्वैरिणीरतः ॥
रंगोपजीवी कथको यश्च प्राकृतनर्तकः ॥ 1.210.40 ॥
1.210.m:
The Brahmin who delights in such a woman is to be known as ‘one who consorts with an unchaste woman’.
[Also unfed are] one who lives by the stage, a professional storyteller, and an ordinary dancer.

1.210.s:
raṃgopajīvī rājeṃdra tathā ca bahuyācakaḥ ..
dve ete nāmanī rājankathakasya prakīrtite ..
kṛtenānena yādṛkca udvṛttaḥ kurunaṃdana .. 41 ..
1.210.d:
रंगोपजीवी राजेंद्र तथा च बहुयाचकः ॥
द्वे एते नामनी राजन्कथकस्य प्रकीर्तिते ॥
कृतेनानेन यादृक्च उद्वृत्तः कुरुनंदन ॥ 41 ॥
1.210.m:
‘One who lives by the stage’, O emperor, and likewise ‘a persistent beggar’—
these two names are proclaimed for the professional storyteller.
Whatever transgressions he has committed thereby, O joy of the Kurus,

1.210.s:
yaḥ stutiṃ gāyate vipraḥ proccaistu janasaṃsadi ..
raṃgopajīvī proktoyaṃ dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ .. 42 ..
1.210.d:
यः स्तुतिं गायते विप्रः प्रोच्चैस्तु जनसंसदि ॥
रंगोपजीवी प्रोक्तोयं द्वितीयः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 42 ॥
1.210.m:
a Brahmin who loudly sings praise in an assembly of people
is proclaimed as ‘one who lives by the stage’; he is declared as the second [type].

1.210.s:
sūcanaṃ kathanaṃ proktaṃ sarvaśāstreṣu bhārata ..
sūcayedyastu ṛkṣāṇi sa vai nakṣatrasūcakaḥ .. 43 ..
1.210.d:
सूचनं कथनं प्रोक्तं सर्वशास्त्रेषु भारत ॥
सूचयेद्यस्तु ऋक्षाणि स वै नक्षत्रसूचकः ॥ 43 ॥
1.210.m:
‘Indication’ is declared to be declaration in all treatises, O Bhārata;
he who points out the lunar mansions is indeed a professional astrologer (nakṣatrasūcaka).

1.210.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ bhavato yaddvijānprati ..
vedāṃgaṃ jyotiḥśāstraṃ tu ṣaṣṭhaṃ proktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ .. 44 ..
1.210.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
अहो बत महत्कष्टं भवतो यद्द्विजान्प्रति ॥
वेदांगं ज्योतिःशास्त्रं तु षष्ठं प्रोक्तं मनीषिभिः ॥ 44 ॥
1.210.m:
Śatānīka said:
Alas, this is indeed a great hardship toward the twice-born that you proclaim!
For astrology is declared by the wise to be the sixth limb of the Veda.

1.210.s:
ṣaḍaṃgo na bhavettena rahitena dvijena ca ..
abhojye paṭhanāttasya yadvatsyādbrāhmaṇo dvija .. 45 ..
1.210.d:
षडंगो न भवेत्तेन रहितेन द्विजेन च ॥
अभोज्ये पठनात्तस्य यद्वत्स्याद्ब्राह्मणो द्विज ॥ 45 ॥
1.210.m:
A twice-born without it would not possess the six limbs.
How can a Brahmin become unfit to be fed on account of studying it, O twice-born?

1.210.s:
bhojyo'khaṇḍaṃ yayau vipro'narthakena tvanarthakam..
vimṛśya kathyatāṃ vipra atra me saṃśayo mahān .. 46 ..
1.210.d:
भोज्योऽखण्डं ययौ विप्रोऽनर्थकेन त्वनर्थकम्॥
विमृश्य कथ्यतां विप्र अत्र मे संशयो महान् ॥ 46 ॥
1.210.m:
If a Brahmin [otherwise] whole became unfit to be fed on account of what is meaningless—
having reflected upon this, O Brahmin, please tell me; herein lies my great doubt.

1.210.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
sādhu pṛṣṭosmi bhavatā śrūyatāmatra nirṇayaḥ ..
yasya jīvyamidaṃ jñeyamaṃgaṃ viprasya vai bhavet .. 47 ..
1.210.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
साधु पृष्टोस्मि भवता श्रूयतामत्र निर्णयः ॥
यस्य जीव्यमिदं ज्ञेयमंगं विप्रस्य वै भवेत् ॥ 47 ॥
1.210.m:
Sumantu said:
You have asked well; hear the resolution in this matter.
When this limb becomes a livelihood for a Brahmin,

1.210.s:
sāṃvatsareṇa jyotiṣā jñānanakṣatrasūcakaḥ ..
na sa bhojyo bhavedrājanyasyeyaṃ jīvikā bhavet .. 48..
1.210.d:
सांवत्सरेण ज्योतिषा ज्ञाननक्षत्रसूचकः ॥
न स भोज्यो भवेद्राजन्यस्येयं जीविका भवेत् ॥ 48॥
1.210.m:
and through calendrical astrology he becomes a professional foreteller of constellations,
he should not be fed, O king, if this is his livelihood.

1.210.s:
niṣkāraṇaṃ parāṇāṃ ca parokṣaṃ doṣakīrtanam..
guṇānāṃ ca yathā guptiḥ parivādaparastu saḥ .. 49 ..
1.210.d:
निष्कारणं पराणां च परोक्षं दोषकीर्तनम्॥
गुणानां च यथा गुप्तिः परिवादपरस्तु सः ॥ 49 ॥
1.210.m:
Proclaiming without cause the faults of others in their absence,
and concealing their virtues—he is devoted to calumny.

1.210.s:
brāhmaṇo yastu rājeṃdra vṛttyā karma karoti vai ..
devatāyatane ceha devānāṃ pūjanaṃ tathā .. 1.210.50 ..
1.210.d:
ब्राह्मणो यस्तु राजेंद्र वृत्त्या कर्म करोति वै ॥
देवतायतने चेह देवानां पूजनं तथा ॥ 1.210.50 ॥
1.210.m:
The Brahmin who performs rituals as a livelihood, O emperor,
and likewise the worship of the gods in a temple,

1.210.s:
ādhipatyaṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ ca naivedyasya paraṃtapa ..
sa jñeyo devalo rājanbrāhmaṇo brāhmaṇādhamaḥ .. 51 ..
1.210.d:
आधिपत्यं भक्षणं च नैवेद्यस्य परंतप ॥
स ज्ञेयो देवलो राजन्ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणाधमः ॥ 51 ॥
1.210.m:
superintendence, and the eating of the food offering, O scorcher of foes—
he is to be known as a temple-priest (devala), O king, a degraded Brahmin.

1.210.s:
nādhikārastu viprāṇāṃ bhaumānāṃ devapūjane ..
vṛttyā bharataśārdūla ādhipatye viśeṣataḥ .. 52 ..
1.210.d:
नाधिकारस्तु विप्राणां भौमानां देवपूजने ॥
वृत्त्या भरतशार्दूल आधिपत्ये विशेषतः ॥ 52 ॥
1.210.m:
Terrestrial Brahmins have no authority to worship the gods
as a livelihood, O tiger of the Bharatas, especially in superintendence.

1.210.s:
yastu pūjayate devīṃ brāhmaṇo dravyalobhataḥ ..
vṛttyai kurukulaśreṣṭha sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam .. 53 ..
1.210.d:
यस्तु पूजयते देवीं ब्राह्मणो द्रव्यलोभतः ॥
वृत्त्यै कुरुकुलश्रेष्ठ स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.210.m:
A Brahmin who worships the goddess out of greed for wealth
as a livelihood, O best of the Kuru lineage, goes surely to hell.

1.210.s:
devālayeṣu sarveṣu agnikāryaṃ ca suvrata ..
yaḥ kuryāddravyalobhena adhogatimavāpnuyāt .. 54 ..
1.210.d:
देवालयेषु सर्वेषु अग्निकार्यं च सुव्रत ॥
यः कुर्याद्द्रव्यलोभेन अधोगतिमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 54 ॥
1.210.m:
He who performs the fire-ritual in all temples
out of greed for wealth, O you of noble vows, attains a downward path.

1.210.s:
devālayeṣu sarveṣu varjayitvā śivālayam ..
devānāṃ pūjanaṃ rājannagnikāryeṣu vā vibho .. 55 ..
1.210.d:
देवालयेषु सर्वेषु वर्जयित्वा शिवालयम् ॥
देवानां पूजनं राजन्नग्निकार्येषु वा विभो ॥ 55 ॥
1.210.m:
In all temples, with the exception of a temple of Śiva,
in the worship of the gods or in fire-rituals, O lord,

1.210.s:
adhikāraḥ smṛto rājanbhojakānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ ..
pūjayaṃtastu te devānprāpnuvaṃti parāṃ gatim .. 56 ..
1.210.d:
अधिकारः स्मृतो राजन्भोजकानां न संशयः ॥
पूजयंतस्तु ते देवान्प्राप्नुवंति परां गतिम् ॥ 56 ॥
1.210.m:
the authority is remembered to belong to the Bhojakas, O king, of this there is no doubt.
By worshipping the gods, they attain the supreme state.

1.210.s:
naivedyaṃ bhuñjate yasmādbhojayaṃti ca bhāskaram ..
pūjayaṃti ca devānāṃ divyatantreṇa te gatāḥ .. 57 ..
1.210.d:
नैवेद्यं भुञ्जते यस्माद्भोजयंति च भास्करम् ॥
पूजयंति च देवानां दिव्यतन्त्रेण ते गताः ॥ 57 ॥
1.210.m:
Because they eat the food offering, feed Bhāskara,
and worship the gods by divine tantra, they are elevated.

1.210.s:
pūjayitvā tu vai devānnaivedyaṃ bhakṣya ca prabhoḥ ..
yāṃti te paramaṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo divākaraḥ .. 58 ..
1.210.d:
पूजयित्वा तु वै देवान्नैवेद्यं भक्ष्य च प्रभोः ॥
यांति ते परमं स्थानं यत्र देवो दिवाकरः ॥ 58 ॥
1.210.m:
Having worshipped the gods and eaten the food offering of the Lord,
they go to the supreme abode where the god who makes the day resides.

1.210.s:
brāhmaṇaścāpi taṃ brūyā ttīkṣṇe sati mahāmate ..
evaṃ kariṣye śreyorthaṃ nātmanastava vā vibho .. 59 ..
1.210.d:
ब्राह्मणश्चापि तं ब्रूया त्तीक्ष्णे सति महामते ॥
एवं करिष्ये श्रेयोर्थं नात्मनस्तव वा विभो ॥ 59 ॥
1.210.m:
Even a Brahmin should say to him, when he is intense, O highly intelligent one:
‘In this way I shall act for the sake of spiritual good, not for my own sake or yours, O lord.’

1.210.s:
ityāmaṃtrya tato gacchetsvagṛhaṃ kurunandana ..
tathā pare'hni saṃpūjya devaṃ bhaktyā divākaram .. 1.210.60 ..
1.210.d:
इत्यामंत्र्य ततो गच्छेत्स्वगृहं कुरुनन्दन ॥
तथा परेऽह्नि संपूज्य देवं भक्त्या दिवाकरम् ॥ 1.210.60 ॥
1.210.m:
Having thus taken leave, he should go to his own house, O joy of the Kurus.
Then on the next day, having worshipped the god who makes the day with devotion,

1.210.s:
kṛtvā ca pāvakaṃ rājanbrāhmaṇānbhojayettataḥ ..
śālyodanaṃ tathā mudgaṃ sugandhaṃ mudgameva hi .. 61 ..
1.210.d:
कृत्वा च पावकं राजन्ब्राह्मणान्भोजयेत्ततः ॥
शाल्योदनं तथा मुद्गं सुगन्धं मुद्गमेव हि ॥ 61 ॥
1.210.m:
and having prepared the sacred fire, O king, he should then feed the Brahmins
boiled rice of śāli, and mudga beans, indeed fragrant mudga beans,

1.210.s:
apūpānguḍapūpāṃśca payo dadhi tathā nṛpa ..
etaistu tṛptimāyāti bhāskaro narasattama .. 62 ..
1.210.d:
अपूपान्गुडपूपांश्च पयो दधि तथा नृप ॥
एतैस्तु तृप्तिमायाति भास्करो नरसत्तम ॥ 62 ॥
1.210.m:
cakes and molasses cakes, milk, and curd, O king.
By these, Bhāskara attains satisfaction, O best of men.

1.210.s:
varjyāni bharataśreṣṭha śṛṇu tvaṃ gadato mama ..
kulatthakānmasūrāṃśca niṣpāvādīṃstathaiva ca .. 63 ..
1.210.d:
वर्ज्यानि भरतश्रेष्ठ शृणु त्वं गदतो मम ॥
कुलत्थकान्मसूरांश्च निष्पावादींस्तथैव च ॥ 63 ॥
1.210.m:
Hear from me as I speak of those that are to be avoided, O best of the Bharatas:
horsegram, lentils, and flat beans and the like.

1.210.s:
sisrukaṃ ca tathānyacca rājamāṣāṃstathaiva ca ..
naitāni bhāskare dadyādya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ .. 64..
1.210.d:
सिस्रुकं च तथान्यच्च राजमाषांस्तथैव च ॥
नैतानि भास्करे दद्याद्य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः ॥ 64॥
1.210.m: And likewise sisruka, and others, as well as kidney beans— / one who desires their own welfare should not give these to the Sun.

1.210.s:
durgadhaṃ yacca kaṭukamatyalpaṃ bhāskarasya tu ..
vimiśrāṃstaḍulāṃścāpi na dadyādbhāskarāya vai .. 65 ..
1.210.d:
दुर्गधं यच्च कटुकमत्यल्पं भास्करस्य तु ॥
विमिश्रांस्तडुलांश्चापि न दद्याद्भास्कराय वै ॥ 65 ॥
1.210.m: Whatever is foul-smelling, bitter, or too little for the Sun, / and mixed rice-grains as well, one should never give to the Sun.

1.210.s:
itthaṃ bhojya dvijaṃ rājanprāśayedarkasaṃpuṭam ..
praṇamya śirasā devamudakena samanvitam .. 66 ..
1.210.d:
इत्थं भोज्य द्विजं राजन्प्राशयेदर्कसंपुटम् ॥
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवमुदकेन समन्वितम् ॥ 66 ॥
1.210.m: Having thus fed a twice-born, O king, one should make him consume the arka-capsule / together with water, having bowed one's head to the god.

1.210.s:
gṛhītvā ketanaṃ yastu bhajate'nyatra lokataḥ ..
nāśnaṃti pitarastasya na devā na ca mānavāḥ .. .. 67 ..
1.210.d:
गृहीत्वा केतनं यस्तु भजतेऽन्यत्र लोकतः ॥
नाश्नंति पितरस्तस्य न देवा न च मानवाः ॥ ॥ 67 ॥
1.210.m: Whoever accepts an invitation [to eat] but then partakes elsewhere among people, / neither his ancestors, nor the gods, nor human beings eat [his offerings].

1.210.s:
niṣkramya nagarādrājangatvā pūrvottarāṃ diśam ..
nātyucce nātinīce ca śucau deśe'rkamuttamam .. 68..
1.210.d:
निष्क्रम्य नगराद्राजन्गत्वा पूर्वोत्तरां दिशम् ॥
नात्युच्चे नातिनीचे च शुचौ देशेऽर्कमुत्तमम् ॥ 68॥
1.210.m: Having gone out of the city, O king, and proceeded to the north-eastern direction, / in a pure place neither too high nor too low, [finding] the excellent arka plant

1.210.s:
jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābāho pūjayitvā khagottama..
pūrvottaragatāścaiva tasya śākhā diśannṛpa..69..
1.210.d:
जातं दृष्ट्वा महाबाहो पूजयित्वा खगोत्तम॥
पूर्वोत्तरगताश्चैव तस्य शाखा दिशन्नृप॥69॥
1.210.m: grown there, O mighty-armed one, having worshipped it, O best of birds, / pointing out its branches that extend toward the north-east, O king,

1.210.s:
śākhāyā agrataḥ pātre susūkṣme pallavāśrite..
suśliṣṭe na pṛthagbhūte saṃpūjya gṛhamāvrajet..1.210.70..
1.210.d:
शाखाया अग्रतः पात्रे सुसूक्ष्मे पल्लवाश्रिते॥
सुश्लिष्टे न पृथग्भूते संपूज्य गृहमाव्रजेत्॥1.210.70॥
1.210.m: at the tip of a branch, in an exceedingly delicate container formed of sprouts, / well-joined and not separated, having worshipped it, he should return home.

1.210.s:
snātaḥ pūjya vivasvaṃtamarkapuṣpaiḥ khagottama..
brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā tu arko me prīyatāmiti..71..
1.210.d:
स्नातः पूज्य विवस्वंतमर्कपुष्पैः खगोत्तम॥
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वा तु अर्को मे प्रीयतामिति॥71॥
1.210.m: Bathed, having worshipped Vivasvat with arka flowers, O best of birds, / and having fed brāhmaṇas [with the thought], “May Arka be pleased with me,”

1.210.s:
prāśya maṃtreṇārkapuṭaṃ tato bhuṃjīta
vāgyataḥ .. devasya purato vīra tvaspṛśandaśanaiḥ puṭam .. 72 ..
1.210.d:
प्राश्य मंत्रेणार्कपुटं ततो भुंजीत
वाग्यतः ॥ देवस्य पुरतो वीर त्वस्पृशन्दशनैः पुटम् ॥ 72 ॥
1.210.m: having consumed the arka-capsule with the mantra, he should then eat with restrained speech / in front of the god, O hero, not touching the capsule with his teeth:

1.210.s:
oṃ arkasaṃpuṭa bhadraṃ te bhadraṃ te'rkaṃ sadāstu vai ..
mamāpi kuru bhadraṃ ca prāyaścittaprado bhava .. 73 ..
1.210.d:
ओं अर्कसंपुट भद्रं ते भद्रं तेऽर्कं सदास्तु वै ॥
ममापि कुरु भद्रं च प्रायश्चित्तप्रदो भव ॥ 73 ॥
1.210.m: “Oṃ, hail to you, O arka-capsule! May hail be to Arka always indeed! / Bring auspiciousness to me as well, and be the bestower of expiation!”

1.210.s:
imaṃ maṃtraṃ japanrājansmarannarkaṃ mahāmate ..
sthitvā pūrvamukho brahma vāriṇā sahitaṃ nṛpa.. 74..
1.210.d:
इमं मंत्रं जपन्राजन्स्मरन्नर्कं महामते ॥
स्थित्वा पूर्वमुखो ब्रह्म वारिणा सहितं नृप॥ 74॥
1.210.m: Muttering this mantra, O king, remembering Arka, O high-minded one, / standing facing east, O brāhmaṇa, [taking it] together with water, O king,

1.210.s:
prāśya bhuṃkte ca yo rājansa yāti paramāṃ gatim ..
daṃtairaspṛśya he vīra tatpuṭaṃ cārkasaṃjñitam .. 75 ..
1.210.d:
प्राश्य भुंक्ते च यो राजन्स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
दंतैरस्पृश्य हे वीर तत्पुटं चार्कसंज्ञितम् ॥ 75 ॥
1.210.m: the one who, having consumed it, eats, O king, he attains the supreme state, / not touching with his teeth, O hero, that capsule named arka.

1.210.s:
anena vidhinā bhaktyā kartavyā saptamī sadā ..
yāvadvarṣe mahābāho prītaye'rkasya śraddhayā .. 76 ..
1.210.d:
अनेन विधिना भक्त्या कर्तव्या सप्तमी सदा ॥
यावद्वर्षे महाबाहो प्रीतयेऽर्कस्य श्रद्धया ॥ 76 ॥
1.210.m: According to this rite, with devotion, the saptamī should always be performed / for a year, O mighty-armed one, with faith for the pleasure of Arka.

1.210.s:
yaścemāṃ saptamīṃ kuryādbhāskaraṃ prīṇayannaraḥ ..
tasyākṣayaṃ bhavedvittamacalaṃ sāptapauruṣam .. 77 ..
1.210.d:
यश्चेमां सप्तमीं कुर्याद्भास्करं प्रीणयन्नरः ॥
तस्याक्षयं भवेद्वित्तमचलं साप्तपौरुषम् ॥ 77 ॥
1.210.m: And whatever man should observe this saptamī, pleasing the Sun, / his wealth becomes imperishable and unshakeable for seven generations.

1.210.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca tathā kṣayam ..
kṛtvemāṃ siddhimāyātaḥ kauthumiḥ sahasā gataḥ .. 78 ..
1.210.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं हिरण्यं च तथा क्षयम् ॥
कृत्वेमां सिद्धिमायातः कौथुमिः सहसा गतः ॥ 78 ॥
1.210.m: Gold, silver, copper, and wealth [never suffer] decay. / Having performed this, Kauthumi attained perfection and departed swiftly.

1.210.s:
kuṣṭharogācca vai mukto jayastomo mahīpatiḥ ..
bṛhadbaladhvajaḥ kopī yājñavalkyo 'tha kṛṣṇajaḥ .. 79 ..
1.210.d:
कुष्ठरोगाच्च वै मुक्तो जयस्तोमो महीपतिः ॥
बृहद्बलध्वजः कोपी याज्ञवल्क्यो ऽथ कृष्णजः ॥ 79 ॥
1.210.m: And truly King Jayastoma was freed from the disease of leprosy, / [as were] Bṛhadbaladhvaja, Kopī, Yājñavalkya, and Kṛṣṇaja.

1.210.s:
arkaṃ caiva samārādhya tato'guste'rkasāmyatām ..
iyaṃ dhanyatamā puṇyā saptamī pāpanāśinī .. 1.210.80 ..
1.210.d:
अर्कं चैव समाराध्य ततोऽगुस्तेऽर्कसाम्यताम् ॥
इयं धन्यतमा पुण्या सप्तमी पापनाशिनी ॥ 1.210.80 ॥
1.210.m: And having worshipped Arka, they then attained likeness with Arka. / This is the most blessed, meritorious saptamī, destroying sins,

1.210.s:
paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ rājankurvatāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ..
tasmādeṣā sadā kāryā vidhivacchreyase'nagha .. 81 ..
1.210.d:
पठतां शृण्वतां राजन्कुर्वतां च विशेषतः ॥
तस्मादेषा सदा कार्या विधिवच्छ्रेयसेऽनघ ॥ 81 ॥
1.210.m: especially for those who recite, hear, and perform it, O king. / Therefore, this should always be performed according to rule for welfare, O sinless one.

1.210.s:
.. śatānīka uvāca .. ..
janakādayo yathā siddhiṃ gatā bhānuṃ prapūjya ca ..
śrutaṃ mayā tu bahuśo na śrutaṃ kauthumiryathā .. 82 ..
1.210.d:
॥ शतानीक उवाच ॥ ॥
जनकादयो यथा सिद्धिं गता भानुं प्रपूज्य च ॥
श्रुतं मया तु बहुशो न श्रुतं कौथुमिर्यथा ॥ 82 ॥
1.210.m: Śatānīka said: / How Janaka and others attained perfection having worshipped the Sun / has been heard by me many times, but how Kauthumi [did so] has not been heard.

1.210.s:
siddhiṃ gato'rkamārādhya kuṣṭhānmuktaśca suvrata ..
kaścāsau kauthumirvipraḥ kathaṃ kuṣṭha mavāptavān .. 83 ..
1.210.d:
सिद्धिं गतोऽर्कमाराध्य कुष्ठान्मुक्तश्च सुव्रत ॥
कश्चासौ कौथुमिर्विप्रः कथं कुष्ठ मवाप्तवान् ॥ 83 ॥
1.210.m: Having worshipped Arka, he attained perfection and was freed from leprosy, O one of good vows. / Who was this brāhmaṇa Kauthumi, and how did he contract leprosy?

1.210.s:
kathamārādhayāmāsa bhānuṃ devapatiṃ dvija ..
etanme vipra nikhilaṃ kīrtayasva samāsataḥ .. 84 .. ..
arkasampuṭikāvarṇanam
1.210.d:
कथमाराधयामास भानुं देवपतिं द्विज ॥
एतन्मे विप्र निखिलं कीर्तयस्व समासतः ॥ 84 ॥ ॥
अर्कसम्पुटिकावर्णनम्
1.210.m:
How did he worship the Sun, the lord of gods, O twice-born? / Relate all this to me in brief, O brāhmaṇa.
Description of the Little Arka-Capsule

1.211.s:
.. sumaṃturuvāca .. ..
sādhu pṛṣṭo 'smi rājeṃdra śṛṇuṣva gadato mama ..
āsītpurā mahāvidvānbrāhmaṇaḥ sthānagottamaḥ .. 1 ..
1.211.d:
॥ सुमंतुरुवाच ॥ ॥
साधु पृष्टो ऽस्मि राजेंद्र शृणुष्व गदतो मम ॥
आसीत्पुरा महाविद्वान्ब्राह्मणः स्थानगोत्तमः ॥ 1 ॥
1.211.m: Sumantu said: / I have been well questioned, O king of kings! Listen to me as I speak. / Formerly there lived a highly learned brāhmaṇa, the best among priests of fixed residence.

1.211.s:
sa gataḥ putrasahito janakasyāśramaṃ dvijaḥ ..
tatra vādo' bhavatteṣāṃ viprairanyairnṛpottama .. 2 ..
1.211.d:
स गतः पुत्रसहितो जनकस्याश्रमं द्विजः ॥
तत्र वादो' भवत्तेषां विप्रैरन्यैर्नृपोत्तम ॥ 2 ॥
1.211.m: That twice-born went with his son to the hermitage of Janaka. / There, a dispute took place between them and other brāhmaṇas, O best of kings.

1.211.s:
krodhāviṣṭena vai tatra hataḥ kauthuminā dvijaḥ ..
tena dṛṣṭvā hataṃ vipraṃ tyaktaḥ pitrā sa kauthumiḥ .. 3 ..
1.211.d:
क्रोधाविष्टेन वै तत्र हतः कौथुमिना द्विजः ॥
तेन दृष्ट्वा हतं विप्रं त्यक्तः पित्रा स कौथुमिः ॥ 3 ॥
1.211.m: There a twice-born was slain by Kauthumi, who was overcome by anger. / Having seen that twice-born slain by him, that Kauthumi was abandoned by his father,

1.211.s:
bhrātṛbhiśca mahābāho tathā śiṣṭaiśca kṛtsnaśaḥ ..
pratyuktaḥ sa ca sarvaistu śokaduḥkhasamanvitaḥ .. 4 ..
1.211.d:
भ्रातृभिश्च महाबाहो तथा शिष्टैश्च कृत्स्नशः ॥
प्रत्युक्तः स च सर्वैस्तु शोकदुःखसमन्वितः ॥ 4 ॥
1.211.m: and by his brothers, O mighty-armed one, and likewise by all the virtuous. / And rebuked by all, he was overcome with sorrow and grief.

1.211.s:
tīrthāni sa jagāmātha divyānyāyatanāni ca ..
na ca muktastvasau vipraḥ sahasā brahmahatyayā .. 5 ..
1.211.d:
तीर्थानि स जगामाथ दिव्यान्यायतनानि च ॥
न च मुक्तस्त्वसौ विप्रः सहसा ब्रह्महत्यया ॥ 5 ॥
1.211.m: He then went to sacred bathing-places and divine shrines, / yet that brāhmaṇa was not quickly freed from the slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

1.211.s:
amukte'tha tayā vipre paro vyādhirajāyata ..
karṇanāsāvihīnastu pūyaśoṇitavisravaḥ .. 6 ..
1.211.d:
अमुक्तेऽथ तया विप्रे परो व्याधिरजायत ॥
कर्णनासाविहीनस्तु पूयशोणितविस्रवः ॥ 6 ॥
1.211.m: Then, as the brāhmaṇa was not freed from it, a terrible disease arose: / he was deprived of ears and nose, oozing with pus and blood.

1.211.s:
pṛthivīṃ paryaṭansarvāṃ punarāgātpiturgṛham ..
duḥkhopahatacittastu pitaraṃ vākyamabravīt ..7..
1.211.d:
पृथिवीं पर्यटन्सर्वां पुनरागात्पितुर्गृहम् ॥
दुःखोपहतचित्तस्तु पितरं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥7॥
1.211.m: Wandering over the whole earth, he came again to his father's house. / His mind struck down with grief, he spoke these words to his father:

1.211.s:
pitargatastu tīrthāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
mukto'smi nānayā tāta krūrayā brahmahatyayā .. 8 ..
1.211.d:
पितर्गतस्तु तीर्थानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ॥
मुक्तोऽस्मि नानया तात क्रूरया ब्रह्महत्यया ॥ 8 ॥
1.211.m: “O father, I have gone to sacred bathing-places and holy shrines, / yet I have not been freed, O father, from this cruel slaying of a brāhmaṇa.

1.211.s:
kṛte'pi hi pare tāta prāyaścitte tu me'nagha ..
kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi tātātīva rujo mama .. 9 ..
1.211.d:
कृतेऽपि हि परे तात प्रायश्चित्ते तु मेऽनघ ॥
किं करोमि क्व गच्छामि तातातीव रुजो मम ॥ 9 ॥
