phalaṃ prāpnoti rājeṃdra māsairdvādaśabhiḥ kramāt ..
itthaṃ yajñaphalaṃ prāpya yāti lokāṃstathottamān .. 82 ..
1.216.d:
आदित्ययज्ञस्य तथा राजसूयाश्वमेधयोः ॥
फलं प्राप्नोति राजेंद्र मासैर्द्वादशभिः क्रमात् ॥
इत्थं यज्ञफलं प्राप्य याति लोकांस्तथोत्तमान् ॥ 82 ॥
1.216.m:
as well as of the solar sacrifice, and of the Rājasūya and the horse sacrifice, / he obtains the fruit, O best of kings, through the twelve months in succession.
Having thus obtained the fruit of the sacrifices, he goes to the highest worlds.

1.216.s:
vajravedikasaṃpannaṃ maṇiratnavibhūṣitam ..
vimānamāsthito rājanmodate śakramaṃdire .. 83 ..
1.216.d:
वज्रवेदिकसंपन्नं मणिरत्नविभूषितम् ॥
विमानमास्थितो राजन्मोदते शक्रमंदिरे ॥ 83 ॥
1.216.m: Mounted upon a celestial chariot furnished with diamond altars / and adorned with gems and jewels, O king, he rejoices in the abode of Śakra.

1.216.s:
tataścaṃdrasya bhavane vāruṇe bhavane tataḥ ..
śociṣkeśagṛhe gatvā gaccheccailavile gṛhe .. 84 ..
1.216.d:
ततश्चंद्रस्य भवने वारुणे भवने ततः ॥
शोचिष्केशगृहे गत्वा गच्छेच्चैलविले गृहे ॥ 84 ॥
1.216.m: Then, having gone to the abode of Candra, then to the abode of Varuṇa, / to the house of Śociṣkeśa, he should go to the house of the son of Ilavilā.

1.216.s:
dhiṣaṇasya gṛhaṃ gatvā tataścitraśikhaṃḍinaḥ ..
vṛddhaśravasamāsādya gacchetkaṃjajamaṃdire ..
evameva nṛpaśreṣṭha nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 85 ..
1.216.d:
धिषणस्य गृहं गत्वा ततश्चित्रशिखंडिनः ॥
वृद्धश्रवसमासाद्य गच्छेत्कंजजमंदिरे ॥
एवमेव नृपश्रेष्ठ नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 85 ॥
1.216.m: Having gone to the house of Dhiṣaṇa, then to that of Citraśikhaṇḍin, / reaching Vṛddhaśravas, he should go to the abode of the Lotus-Born. / Thus indeed, best of kings, no hesitation should be made in this matter.

1.216.s:
phalametatsamuddiṣṭaṃ śṛṇvatāṃ satataṃ nṛṇām ..
etatphalaṃ vatsareṇa śṛṇvato vidhito nṛpa .. 86 ..
1.216.d:
फलमेतत्समुद्दिष्टं शृण्वतां सततं नृणाम् ॥
एतत्फलं वत्सरेण शृण्वतो विधितो नृप ॥ 86 ॥
1.216.m: This fruit is declared for men who listen constantly; / this is the fruit for one who listens according to rule for a year, O king.

1.216.s:
etāni parimāṇāni vatsareṇa bhavaṃti vai ..
śṛṇvatāṃ nṛpaśārdūla dadatāṃ vācakāya vai .. 87 ..
1.216.d:
एतानि परिमाणानि वत्सरेण भवंति वै ॥
शृण्वतां नृपशार्दूल ददतां वाचकाय वै ॥ 87 ॥
1.216.m: These measures indeed come to pass in a year, / tiger among kings, for those who listen and give to the reciter.

1.216.s:
ekaṃ ca dve tathā trīṇi catvāri ca viśāṃpate ..
deyāni vācakāyeha māsimāsi narādhipa .. 88 ..
1.216.d:
एकं च द्वे तथा त्रीणि चत्वारि च विशांपते ॥
देयानि वाचकायेह मासिमासि नराधिप ॥ 88 ॥
1.216.m: One, two, three, and four, O lord of the people, / are to be given here to the reciter month by month, O ruler of men,

1.216.s:
brāhmaṇādyairnṛpa śreṣṭha sarvavarṇavibhāgaśaḥ ..
samāpte parvaṇi tathā vācakaṃ pūjayetpunaḥ ..89..
1.216.d:
ब्राह्मणाद्यैर्नृप श्रेष्ठ सर्ववर्णविभागशः ॥
समाप्ते पर्वणि तथा वाचकं पूजयेत्पुनः ॥89॥
1.216.m: by brāhmaṇas and the other castes according to their division, best of kings; / likewise, when the festival is completed, one should worship the reciter again.

1.216.s:
vācakaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ caiva sarvakāmaiḥ prapūjayet ..
gandhamālyādibhirdivyairvā sobhirvividhairapi .. 1.216.90 ..
1.216.d:
वाचकं ब्राह्मणं चैव सर्वकामैः प्रपूजयेत् ॥
गन्धमाल्यादिभिर्दिव्यैर्वा सोभिर्विविधैरपि ॥ 1.216.90 ॥
1.216.m: One should worship the reciter, a brāhmaṇa, with all desired offerings, / with heavenly scents, garlands, and the like, and also with various garments.

1.216.s:
vācakāya pradattvā tu tato viprānprapūjayet ..
hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ rukmaṃ gāśca kāṃsyopadohanāḥ ..91..
1.216.d:
वाचकाय प्रदत्त्वा तु ततो विप्रान्प्रपूजयेत् ॥
हिरण्यं रजतं रुक्मं गाश्च कांस्योपदोहनाः ॥91॥
1.216.m: Having given first to the reciter, one should then worship the brāhmaṇas / with gold, silver, gold coins, and cows that have bronze milking pails.

1.216.s:
dattvā ca vācakāyeha śrutasya prāpyate phalam ..
yathā sadakṣiṇaṃ cānnaṃ śrāddhakāle prakīrtitam ..
tathā śrutaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭha sadakṣiṇamudāhṛtam .. 92 ..
1.216.d:
दत्त्वा च वाचकायेह श्रुतस्य प्राप्यते फलम् ॥
यथा सदक्षिणं चान्नं श्राद्धकाले प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
तथा श्रुतं नृपश्रेष्ठ सदक्षिणमुदाहृतम् ॥ 92 ॥
1.216.m: And having given to the reciter here, the fruit of what was heard is obtained; / just as food given at the time of a śrāddha is proclaimed to be accompanied by a sacrificial fee, / even so what is heard, best of kings, is declared to be accompanied by a sacrificial fee.

1.216.s:
vācakaṃ pūjayedyasmā tpaścāllekhakapūjanam ..
samāpte parvaṇi vibho viśeṣeṇaiva cārcayet .. 93 ..
1.216.d:
वाचकं पूजयेद्यस्मा त्पश्चाल्लेखकपूजनम् ॥
समाप्ते पर्वणि विभो विशेषेणैव चार्चयेत् ॥ 93 ॥
1.216.m: Since one should worship the reciter, after that comes the worship of the scribe; / when the festival is completed, O lord, one should worship him especially.

1.216.s:
vācakaḥ pūjito yena pūjitāstena devatāḥ ..
vācake parituṣṭe ca mama prītiranuttamā ..94..
1.216.d:
वाचकः पूजितो येन पूजितास्तेन देवताः ॥
वाचके परितुष्टे च मम प्रीतिरनुत्तमा ॥94॥
1.216.m: By him by whom the reciter is worshipped, the deities are worshipped; / and when the reciter is fully pleased, my delight is unsurpassed.

1.216.s:
iti vedhāḥ sadā prāha devānāṃ purataḥ purā ..
tasmiṃstuṣṭe jagatsarvaṃ tuṣṭaṃ bhavati nityaśaḥ....
tasmātprapūjayedvipra vācakaṃ nṛpa sattama ..
na tulyaṃ vācakeneha pātradānasya vidyate..96..
1.216.d:
इति वेधाः सदा प्राह देवानां पुरतः पुरा ॥
तस्मिंस्तुष्टे जगत्सर्वं तुष्टं भवति नित्यशः॥॥
तस्मात्प्रपूजयेद्विप्र वाचकं नृप सत्तम ॥
न तुल्यं वाचकेनेह पात्रदानस्य विद्यते॥96॥
1.216.m: Thus the Creator always spoke before the gods of old: / 'When he is pleased, the entire world is constantly pleased; / therefore one should worship the brāhmaṇa reciter, best of kings; / there is no recipient of gifts equal to the reciter in this world.

1.216.s:
tiṣṭhaṃti yasya śāstrāṇi jihvāgre pṛthivīpate..
dṛṣṭaśca gocarastāta kastena sadṛśo dvijaḥ..97..
1.216.d:
तिष्ठंति यस्य शास्त्राणि जिह्वाग्रे पृथिवीपते॥
दृष्टश्च गोचरस्तात कस्तेन सदृशो द्विजः॥97॥
1.216.m: On the tip of whose tongue the scriptures reside, O lord of the earth, / and who has seen what lies within their scope, dear one, what twice-born man is equal to him?

1.216.s:
na tulyaṃ vidyate tena bhuvi pātraṃ nareṣu vai ..
tasmādannaṃ sadā pūrvaṃ tasmai deyaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
śrāddhe yasya dvijo bhuṃkte vācakaḥ śradayānvitaḥ ..
bhavaṃti pitarastasya tṛptā varṣaśataṃ nṛpa ..98..
1.216.d:
न तुल्यं विद्यते तेन भुवि पात्रं नरेषु वै ॥
तस्मादन्नं सदा पूर्वं तस्मै देयं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
श्राद्धे यस्य द्विजो भुंक्ते वाचकः श्रदयान्वितः ॥
भवंति पितरस्तस्य तृप्ता वर्षशतं नृप ॥98॥
1.216.m: No recipient among men on earth is found equal to him; / therefore the wise know that food should always be given to him first. / At whose śrāddha the twice-born reciter eats endowed with faith, / his ancestors remain satisfied for a hundred years, O king.

1.216.s:
yatheha sarvadevānāṃ bhāskaraḥ pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
vispaṣṭamadbhutaṃ śāṃtaṃ spaṣṭākṣarapadaṃ tathā ..
kalasvarasamāyuktaṃ rasabhāvasamanvitam .. 99 ..
1.216.d:
यथेह सर्वदेवानां भास्करः प्रवरः स्मृतः ॥
विस्पष्टमद्भुतं शांतं स्पष्टाक्षरपदं तथा ॥
कलस्वरसमायुक्तं रसभावसमन्वितम् ॥ 99 ॥
1.216.m: Just as the Sun is recalled as the foremost of all the gods here, / [so is he who recites] distinctly, wondrously, calmly, with clear syllables and words, / endowed with a sweet tone, accompanied by aesthetic flavor and emotion,

1.216.s:
budhyamānaḥ sadātyarthaṃ graṃthāthaṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa ..
brāhmaṇādiṣu varṇeṣu graṃthārthaṃ vācayennṛpa .. 1.216.100 ..
1.216.d:
बुध्यमानः सदात्यर्थं ग्रंथाथं कृत्स्नशो नृप ॥
ब्राह्मणादिषु वर्णेषु ग्रंथार्थं वाचयेन्नृप ॥ 1.216.100 ॥
1.216.m: always understanding the meaning of the text exceedingly well in its entirety, O king; / he should recite the meaning of the text among the castes beginning with the brāhmaṇas, O king.

1.216.s:
ya evaṃ vācayedrājanya vipro vyāsa ucyate ..
ato'nyathā kathayitā jñeyo'sau vaktṛnāmakaḥ .. 101 ..
1.216.d:
य एवं वाचयेद्राजन्य विप्रो व्यास उच्यते ॥
अतोऽन्यथा कथयिता ज्ञेयोऽसौ वक्तृनामकः ॥ 101 ॥
1.216.m: The brāhmaṇa who recites in this manner, O king, is called a Vyāsa; / one who relates otherwise should be known merely by the name of speaker.

1.216.s:
itthaṃbhūto vasedyasminvācako vyāsasannibhaḥ ..
deśe'tha pattane rājansa deśaḥ pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 102 ..
1.216.d:
इत्थंभूतो वसेद्यस्मिन्वाचको व्याससन्निभः ॥
देशेऽथ पत्तने राजन्स देशः प्रवरः स्मृतः ॥ 102 ॥
1.216.m: In whichever country or city such a reciter, like unto Vyāsa, should dwell, / O king, that country is recalled as foremost.

1.216.s:
te dhanyāste mahātmānaste kṛtārthā na saṃśayaḥ ..
vasaṃti yatnato yasminsa deśaḥ pravaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 103 ..
1.216.d:
ते धन्यास्ते महात्मानस्ते कृतार्था न संशयः ॥
वसंति यत्नतो यस्मिन्स देशः प्रवरः स्मृतः ॥ 103 ॥
1.216.m: They are fortunate, they are great-souled, they have achieved their purpose—there is no doubt— / who dwell with effort where he lives; that country is recalled as foremost.

1.216.s:
na śobhate puraṃ vīra vyāsahīnaṃ kadācana ..
yathārkahīnaṃ hi dinaṃ caṃdrahīnā yathā niśā .. 104 ..
1.216.d:
न शोभते पुरं वीर व्यासहीनं कदाचन ॥
यथार्कहीनं हि दिनं चंद्रहीना यथा निशा ॥ 104 ॥
1.216.m: A city without a Vyāsa never shines, O hero, / just as a day without the sun, or a night without the moon.

1.216.s:
na rājate saro yadvatpadminī rahitaṃ nṛpa ..
tathā vyāsavihīnaṃ tu rājate na puraṃ kvacit .. 105 ..
1.216.d:
न राजते सरो यद्वत्पद्मिनी रहितं नृप ॥
तथा व्यासविहीनं तु राजते न पुरं क्वचित् ॥ 105 ॥
1.216.m: Just as a lake does not look splendid without a lotus plant, O king, / even so a city devoid of a Vyāsa never looks splendid anywhere.

1.216.s:
praṇamya vācakaṃ bhaktyā yatphalaṃ prāpyate naraiḥ ..
na tatkratusahasreṇa prāpyate kurunaṃdana .. 1 0 6 ..
1.216.d:
प्रणम्य वाचकं भक्त्या यत्फलं प्राप्यते नरैः ॥
न तत्क्रतुसहस्रेण प्राप्यते कुरुनंदन ॥ 1 0 6 ॥
1.216.m: The fruit that is obtained by men having bowed with devotion to the reciter / cannot be obtained by a thousand sacrifices, O delight of the Kurus.

1.216.s:
yathaikato grahāḥ sarve ekatastu divākaraḥ ..
tathaikato dvijāḥ sarve ekatastu sa vācakaḥ .. 107 ..
1.216.d:
यथैकतो ग्रहाः सर्वे एकतस्तु दिवाकरः ॥
तथैकतो द्विजाः सर्वे एकतस्तु स वाचकः ॥ 107 ॥
1.216.m: Just as on one side are all the planets and on the other is the Sun, / so on one side are all twice-born men and on the other is the reciter.

1.216.s:
yathā vedasamo nāsti āgamo bhuvi kaścana ..
tathā vyāsasamo nāsti brāhmaṇo bhuvi kaścana .. 108 ..
1.216.d:
यथा वेदसमो नास्ति आगमो भुवि कश्चन ॥
तथा व्याससमो नास्ति ब्राह्मणो भुवि कश्चन ॥ 108 ॥
1.216.m: Just as there is no traditional scripture on earth equal to the Veda, / so there is no brāhmaṇa on earth equal to a Vyāsa.

1.216.s:
kurukṣetrasamaṃ tīrthaṃ na dvitīyaṃ pracakṣate ..
na nadī gaṃgayā tulyā na devo bhāskarādvaraḥ ..109..
1.216.d:
कुरुक्षेत्रसमं तीर्थं न द्वितीयं प्रचक्षते ॥
न नदी गंगया तुल्या न देवो भास्कराद्वरः ॥109॥
1.216.m: They declare that there is no second sacred place equal to Kurukṣetra; / there is no river equal to the Gaṅgā, and no god superior to the Sun.

1.216.s:
nāśvamedhasamaṃ puṇyaṃ na pāpaṃ brahmahatyayā ..
putrajanmasukhaistulyaṃ na sukhaṃ vidyate yathā ..1.216.11 0..
1.216.d:
नाश्वमेधसमं पुण्यं न पापं ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
पुत्रजन्मसुखैस्तुल्यं न सुखं विद्यते यथा ॥1.216.11 0॥
1.216.m: There is no merit equal to the horse sacrifice, no sin equal to the killing of a brāhmaṇa, / and just as there is no pleasure equal to the pleasures from the birth of a son,

1.216.s:
tathā vyāsasamo vipro na kvacitprāpyate nṛpa ..
daive karmaṇi pitrye ca pāvanaḥ paramo nṛṇām .. 111 ..
1.216.d:
तथा व्याससमो विप्रो न क्वचित्प्राप्यते नृप ॥
दैवे कर्मणि पित्र्ये च पावनः परमो नृणाम् ॥ 111 ॥
1.216.m: even so a brāhmaṇa equal to a Vyāsa is found nowhere, O king; / in rites for the gods and in rites for the ancestors, he is the supreme purifier of men.

1.216.s:
nāsti vyāsasamaḥ śreṣṭha itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ ..
atha viprasahasrāṇāṃ vipro'yaṃ śreṣṭha īritaḥ ..
upaviṣṭo yadā bhuṃkte vyāso vai vipramaṇḍale ..112..
1.216.d:
नास्ति व्याससमः श्रेष्ठ इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥
अथ विप्रसहस्राणां विप्रोऽयं श्रेष्ठ ईरितः ॥
उपविष्टो यदा भुंक्ते व्यासो वै विप्रमण्डले ॥112॥
1.216.m: 'There is none equal to a Vyāsa, he is the best'—such is this Vedic revelation. / Now among thousands of brāhmaṇas, this brāhmaṇa is declared the foremost; / when a Vyāsa sits and eats in a gathering of brāhmaṇas,

1.216.s:
śrāddhe tāta pavitrāṇi kathitāni purā mama..
brahmaṇā rājaśārdūla śṛṇu tāni yathāvidhi ..113..
1.216.d:
श्राद्धे तात पवित्राणि कथितानि पुरा मम॥
ब्रह्मणा राजशार्दूल शृणु तानि यथाविधि ॥113॥
1.216.m: the purifying items at a śrāddha were told to me of old, dear one, / by Brahmā, O tiger among kings; hear them according to rule:

1.216.s:
madhu pāyasaṃ kālaśākastilāśca kutapastathā ..
rājataṃ cāpi pātreṣu brāhmaṇeṣvatha vācakaḥ ..114..
1.216.d:
मधु पायसं कालशाकस्तिलाश्च कुतपस्तथा ॥
राजतं चापि पात्रेषु ब्राह्मणेष्वथ वाचकः ॥114॥
1.216.m: honey, rice pudding, black mustard greens, sesame seeds, and the kutapa hour, / and silver among vessels, and the reciter among brāhmaṇas.

1.216.s:
daive karmaṇi pitrye ca sa jñeyaḥ paṃktipāvanaḥ ..
vācakaśca yatiścaiva tathā yaśca ṣaḍaṃgavit .. 115 ..
1.216.d:
दैवे कर्मणि पित्र्ये च स ज्ञेयः पंक्तिपावनः ॥
वाचकश्च यतिश्चैव तथा यश्च षडंगवित् ॥ 115 ॥
1.216.m: In rites for the gods and in rites for the ancestors, he should be known as one who purifies the row; / the reciter, the ascetic, and he who knows the six auxiliaries of the Veda—

1.216.s:
ete sarve nṛpaśreṣṭha vijñeyāḥ paṃktipāvanāḥ ..
nāmanī vācakasyaite śṛṅgavārthamathaitayoḥ .. 116 ..
1.216.d:
एते सर्वे नृपश्रेष्ठ विज्ञेयाः पंक्तिपावनाः ॥
नामनी वाचकस्यैते शृङ्गवार्थमथैतयोः ॥ 116 ॥
1.216.m: all these, best of kings, are to be known as purifiers of the row. / These are the two names of the reciter; now hear the meaning of both:

1.216.s:
itihāsapurāṇāni jayeti viditāni vai ..
upajīvati yasmādvai vācayāno dvijo nṛpa ..
jayopajīvī tenāsau gataḥ khyātiṃ tu vācakaḥ .. 117 ..
1.216.d:
इतिहासपुराणानि जयेति विदितानि वै ॥
उपजीवति यस्माद्वै वाचयानो द्विजो नृप ॥
जयोपजीवी तेनासौ गतः ख्यातिं तु वाचकः ॥ 117 ॥
1.216.m: the histories and purāṇas are indeed known as 'Jaya'; / since the twice-born man makes his living by reciting them, O king, / that reciter has therefore attained renown as 'living by Jaya'.

1.216.s:
vispaṣṭamadbhutaṃ śāṃtaṃ spaṣṭākṣaramidaṃ tathā ..
kalasvarasamāyuktaṃ rasabhāvasamanvitam..118..
1.216.d:
विस्पष्टमद्भुतं शांतं स्पष्टाक्षरमिदं तथा ॥
कलस्वरसमायुक्तं रसभावसमन्वितम्॥118॥
1.216.m: Distinctly, wondrously, calmly, with this text having clear syllables, / endowed with a sweet tone, accompanied by aesthetic flavor and emotion,

1.216.s:
yudhyamānotha vātyarthaṃ graṃthārthaṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa ..
brāhmaṇādiṣu varṇeṣu graṃthārthaṃ cārpayettathā .. 119 ..
1.216.d:
युध्यमानोथ वात्यर्थं ग्रंथार्थं कृत्स्नशो नृप ॥
ब्राह्मणादिषु वर्णेषु ग्रंथार्थं चार्पयेत्तथा ॥ 119 ॥
1.216.m: or grasping exceedingly well the meaning of the text in its entirety, O king, / he should also impart the meaning of the text among the castes beginning with the brāhmaṇas.

1.216.s:
ya evaṃ vācayedrājanya vipro vyāsa ucyate ..
ato'nyathā vācayitā na gacchedvyāsatāṃ kvacit .. 1.216.120 ..
1.216.d:
य एवं वाचयेद्राजन्य विप्रो व्यास उच्यते ॥
अतोऽन्यथा वाचयिता न गच्छेद्व्यासतां क्वचित् ॥ 1.216.120 ॥
1.216.m: The brāhmaṇa who recites in this manner, O king, is called a Vyāsa; / one who recites otherwise would never attain the status of a Vyāsa.

1.216.s:
trividhaṃ vācakaṃ vidyātsadā guṇavibhedataḥ ..
śrāvakaṃ ca mahābāho trividhaṃ guṇabhedataḥ .. 121 ..
1.216.d:
त्रिविधं वाचकं विद्यात्सदा गुणविभेदतः ॥
श्रावकं च महाबाहो त्रिविधं गुणभेदतः ॥ 121 ॥
1.216.m: One should know the reciter to be of three kinds, according to the distinction of the guṇas; / and the hearer, O mighty-armed one, is of three kinds according to the distinction of the guṇas.

1.216.s:
dvāvetau kathyamānau tu nibodha gadato mama ..
abhidrutaṃ tathāspaṣṭaṃ vistaraṃ svaravarjitam ..122..
1.216.d:
द्वावेतौ कथ्यमानौ तु निबोध गदतो मम ॥
अभिद्रुतं तथास्पष्टं विस्तरं स्वरवर्जितम् ॥122॥
1.216.m: As these two are being described, understand from me as I speak: / hurried, indistinct, diffuse, devoid of tone,

1.216.s:
padacchedavihīnaṃ ca tathā bhāvavivarjitam ..
abudhyamāno graṃthārthamabhīṣṭotsāhavarjitaḥ .. 123 ..
1.216.d:
पदच्छेदविहीनं च तथा भावविवर्जितम् ॥
अबुध्यमानो ग्रंथार्थमभीष्टोत्साहवर्जितः ॥ 123 ॥
1.216.m: lacking word separation, devoid of feeling, / not understanding the meaning of the text, devoid of desirable enthusiasm—

1.216.s:
īdṛśaṃ vācayedyastu vācakaḥ kṣmādhipeśvara ..
krodhano'priyavādī ca ajñānādgraṃthadūṣakaḥ .. 124 ..
1.216.d:
ईदृशं वाचयेद्यस्तु वाचकः क्ष्माधिपेश्वर ॥
क्रोधनोऽप्रियवादी च अज्ञानाद्ग्रंथदूषकः ॥ 124 ॥
1.216.m: a reciter who recites in such a way, O lord of rulers of the earth, / wrathful, speaking unkind words, and corrupting the text through ignorance,

1.216.s:
budhyate na ca kaṣṭācca sa jñeyo vācakādhamaḥ ..
vispaṣṭamadbhutaṃ śāṃtaṃ rasabhāvasamanvitam.. 125 ..
1.216.d:
बुध्यते न च कष्टाच्च स ज्ञेयो वाचकाधमः ॥
विस्पष्टमद्भुतं शांतं रसभावसमन्वितम्॥ 125 ॥
1.216.m: and does not understand it even with difficulty, he should be known as the lowest of reciters. / Distinctly, wonderfully, calmly, endowed with aesthetic flavor and emotion,

1.216.s:
abudhyamāno graṃthārthaṃ vācayedyastu vācakaḥ ..
sa jñeyo rājaso rājannidānīṃ sāttvikaṃ śṛṇu .. 126 ..
1.216.d:
अबुध्यमानो ग्रंथार्थं वाचयेद्यस्तु वाचकः ॥
स ज्ञेयो राजसो राजन्निदानीं सात्त्विकं शृणु ॥ 126 ॥
1.216.m: yet not understanding the meaning of the text—the reciter who recites thus / should be known as passionate, O king. Now hear about the virtuous one:

1.216.s:
vispaṣṭamadbhutaṃ śāṃtaṃ spaṣṭākṣarapadaṃ tathā ..
kalasvarasamāyuktaṃ rasabhāvasamanvitam ..127 ..
1.216.d:
विस्पष्टमद्भुतं शांतं स्पष्टाक्षरपदं तथा ॥
कलस्वरसमायुक्तं रसभावसमन्वितम् ॥127 ॥
1.216.m: Distinctly, wonderfully, calmly, with syllables and words clearly articulated, / accompanied by a melodious tone, endowed with aesthetic flavor and emotion,

1.216.s:
attyarthaṃ budhyamānastu graṃthārthaṃ kṛtsnaśo nṛpa ..
brāhmaṇādiṣu varṇeṣu ācāryo vidhivannṛpa .. 128 ..
1.216.d:
अत्त्यर्थं बुध्यमानस्तु ग्रंथार्थं कृत्स्नशो नृप ॥
ब्राह्मणादिषु वर्णेषु आचार्यो विधिवन्नृप ॥ 128 ॥
1.216.m: deeply understanding the meaning of the text in its entirety, O king, / an ācārya according to rule among the social classes beginning with the brahmins, O king,

1.216.s:
ya evaṃ vācayedrājansa jñeyaḥ sāttviko budhaiḥ ..
śraddhā bhaktivihīno yo lobhiṣṭhaḥ kaṭuko yathā .. 129 ..
1.216.d:
य एवं वाचयेद्राजन्स ज्ञेयः सात्त्विको बुधैः ॥
श्रद्धा भक्तिविहीनो यो लोभिष्ठः कटुको यथा ॥ 129 ॥
1.216.m: he who recites in this manner, O king, should be known by the wise as virtuous. / He who is devoid of faith and devotion, excessively greedy, harsh,

1.216.s:
hetuvādaparo rājaṃstathāsūyāsamanvitaḥ ..
nityāṃ naimittikāṃ kāmyāmādadaddakṣiṇāṃ nṛpa .. .. 1.216.130 ..
1.216.d:
हेतुवादपरो राजंस्तथासूयासमन्वितः ॥
नित्यां नैमित्तिकां काम्यामाददद्दक्षिणां नृप ॥ ॥ 1.216.130 ॥
1.216.m: intent on contentious debate, O king, and full of malice, / taking regular, occasional, and desire-prompted sacrificial gifts, O king—

1.216.s:
vācako yo mahābāho śṛṇuyādyastu mānavaḥ ..
sa jñeyastāmaso rājañchrāvako mānavo'pi saḥ .. 131 ..
1.216.d:
वाचको यो महाबाहो शृणुयाद्यस्तु मानवः ॥
स ज्ञेयस्तामसो राजञ्छ्रावको मानवोऽपि सः ॥ 131 ॥
1.216.m: such a reciter, O mighty-armed one, and the man who listens to him, / should be known as dark, O king; and that human listener too [is dark].

1.216.s:
na tasya purato vīra vācaye tprājña eva hi ..
prasaṃgācchṛṇuyādyastu śraddhābhaktivivarjitaḥ .. 132..
1.216.d:
न तस्य पुरतो वीर वाचये त्प्राज्ञ एव हि ॥
प्रसंगाच्छृणुयाद्यस्तु श्रद्धाभक्तिविवर्जितः ॥ 132॥
1.216.m: A wise man should never recite before him, O hero. / But he who listens merely out of circumstance, devoid of faith and devotion,

1.216.s:
rājankautukapātraṃ tu sa jñeyo rājaso bhavet ..
saṃtyajya sarvakāryāṇi bhaktyā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ .. 133 ..
1.216.d:
राजन्कौतुकपात्रं तु स ज्ञेयो राजसो भवेत् ॥
संत्यज्य सर्वकार्याणि भक्त्या श्रद्धासमन्वितः ॥ 133 ॥
1.216.m: an object of curiosity, O king, he should be known as passionate. / Setting aside all tasks, with devotion and endowed with faith,

1.216.s:
satataṃ pūjayedyastu vācakaṃ śraddhayā mudā ..
nitye naimittike kāmye gurūnvai devatāstathā .. 134 ..
1.216.d:
सततं पूजयेद्यस्तु वाचकं श्रद्धया मुदा ॥
नित्ये नैमित्तिके काम्ये गुरून्वै देवतास्तथा ॥ 134 ॥
1.216.m: he who constantly honors the reciter with faith and joy / in regular, occasional, and desire-prompted [rites], as he would the gurus and deities,

1.216.s:
ya evaṃ śṛṇuyādvīra sa jñeyaḥ sāttviko budhaiḥ ..
vyāsaḥ pūjyaḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ yathā vyāsavaco nṛpa.. 135 ..
1.216.d:
य एवं शृणुयाद्वीर स ज्ञेयः सात्त्विको बुधैः ॥
व्यासः पूज्यः श्रावकाणां यथा व्यासवचो नृप॥ 135 ॥
1.216.m: he who listens in this way, O hero, is known by the wise as virtuous. / A Vyāsa is to be honored by listeners just as the word of Vyāsa [is], O king.

1.216.s:
tasmātpūjyatamo nānyaḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ nṛpottama ..
yataḥ sa vai gurusteṣāṃ jñānadātā sadā nṛpa ..136..
1.216.d:
तस्मात्पूज्यतमो नान्यः श्रावकाणां नृपोत्तम ॥
यतः स वै गुरुस्तेषां ज्ञानदाता सदा नृप ॥136॥
1.216.m: Therefore none is more worthy of worship for listeners than he, O best of kings, / since he is their guru, always the giver of knowledge, O king.

1.216.s:
caturṇāmiha varṇānāṃ nānyo bandhuḥ pracakṣyate ..
vyāsādṛte nṛpaśreṣṭha itīyaṃ vaidikī śrutiḥ ..137..
1.216.d:
चतुर्णामिह वर्णानां नान्यो बन्धुः प्रचक्ष्यते ॥
व्यासादृते नृपश्रेष्ठ इतीयं वैदिकी श्रुतिः ॥137॥
1.216.m: No other kin in this world is proclaimed for the four classes / besides a Vyāsa, O best of kings; such is this Vedic revelation.

1.216.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayedvācakaṃ sadā ..
sa guruḥ sa pitā mātā sa baṃdhuḥ sa suhṛttathā .. 138 ..
1.216.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजयेद्वाचकं सदा ॥
स गुरुः स पिता माता स बंधुः स सुहृत्तथा ॥ 138 ॥
1.216.m: Therefore, with every effort one should constantly honor the reciter; / he is the guru, he is the father, mother, he is the kinsman, and he is the friend.

1.216.s:
vācako nṛpaśārdūla viprādīnāmaśeṣataḥ ..
itthaṃ vyāso gururjñeyaḥ pūjyo mānyo dvijātibhiḥ .. 139 ..
1.216.d:
वाचको नृपशार्दूल विप्रादीनामशेषतः ॥
इत्थं व्यासो गुरुर्ज्ञेयः पूज्यो मान्यो द्विजातिभिः ॥ 139 ॥
1.216.m: The reciter, O tiger among kings, [is all these] to all the brahmins and others without remainder. / Thus a Vyāsa should be recognized as a guru, to be worshipped and respected by the twice-born.

1.216.s:
śṛṇvaṃti ye narā rājansa teṣāṃ gururucyate ..
pūjārthaṃ tasya samayaḥ śrāvakāṇāmudāhṛtaḥ .. . 1.216.140 ..
1.216.d:
शृण्वंति ये नरा राजन्स तेषां गुरुरुच्यते ॥
पूजार्थं तस्य समयः श्रावकाणामुदाहृतः ॥ । 1.216.140 ॥
1.216.m: The men who listen, O king, of them he is called the guru. / The proper time has been declared for listeners to perform his worship:

1.216.s:
ye śṛṇvaṃti nṛpaśreṣṭha māsi māsi dadaṃti te ..
svarṇamāṣakamekasmai vācakāya pṛthakpṛthak ..141..
1.216.d:
ये शृण्वंति नृपश्रेष्ठ मासि मासि ददंति ते ॥
स्वर्णमाषकमेकस्मै वाचकाय पृथक्पृथक् ॥141॥
1.216.m: Those who listen, O best of kings, give month by month / one gold māṣaka individually to each reciter.

1.216.s:
dvādaśyāṃ cāmāvāsyāyāmatha vā ravisaṃkrame ..
sā nityā dakṣiṇā tasyāṃ yā ca śreyo'rthamātmanaḥ..142..
1.216.d:
द्वादश्यां चामावास्यायामथ वा रविसंक्रमे ॥
सा नित्या दक्षिणा तस्यां या च श्रेयोऽर्थमात्मनः॥142॥
1.216.m: On the twelfth lunar day, on the new moon day, or at a solar transit, / that is the regular priestly gift, and that which is for his own welfare.

1.216.s:
ayane viṣuve caiva caṃdrasūryagrahe tathā ..
prāpte vāparapakṣe ca dānaṃ tasyai svaśaktitaḥ .. 143 ..
1.216.d:
अयने विषुवे चैव चंद्रसूर्यग्रहे तथा ॥
प्राप्ते वापरपक्षे च दानं तस्यै स्वशक्तितः ॥ 143 ॥
1.216.m: At a solstice, at an equinox, at an eclipse of the moon or sun, / or when the dark fortnight arrives, a gift [should be given] to him according to one's means.

1.216.s:
deyaṃ syācchrāvakaistāta taṃ muktvā nānyato nṛpa ..
prathamaṃ tasya dātavyaṃ śreyo'rthaṃ śrāvakaiḥ sadā ..144..
1.216.d:
देयं स्याच्छ्रावकैस्तात तं मुक्त्वा नान्यतो नृप ॥
प्रथमं तस्य दातव्यं श्रेयोऽर्थं श्रावकैः सदा ॥144॥
1.216.m: It should be given by the listeners, dear one, to him and to no one else, O king. / First it should be given to him always by the listeners for the sake of welfare.

1.216.s:
adattvā tasya yenyasmai saṃprayacchaṃti śrāvakāḥ ..
avamānaḥ kṛtastaistu vācakasya bhavennṛpa .. 145 ..
1.216.d:
अदत्त्वा तस्य येन्यस्मै संप्रयच्छंति श्रावकाः ॥
अवमानः कृतस्तैस्तु वाचकस्य भवेन्नृप ॥ 145 ॥
1.216.m: Not giving to him, the listeners who give to another— / an insult is thereby committed by them against the reciter, O king.

1.216.s:
kṛtvāvamānamatha taiḥ prāpyate yatphalaṃ nṛpa ..
brāhmaṇādyaiḥ samastaiśca tacchṛṇuṣva varānana ..146..
1.216.d:
कृत्वावमानमथ तैः प्राप्यते यत्फलं नृप ॥
ब्राह्मणाद्यैः समस्तैश्च तच्छृणुष्व वरानन ॥146॥
1.216.m: Having committed an insult, the fruit that is obtained by them, O king, / by all of them beginning with the brahmins, hear that, O fair-faced one:

1.216.s:
śūdratvaṃ brāhmaṇo yāti kṣatriyo yāti kākatām ..
jāyate ca tathā vaiśyaḥ śūdraścāṇḍālatāṃ vrajet ..147..
1.216.d:
शूद्रत्वं ब्राह्मणो याति क्षत्रियो याति काकताम् ॥
जायते च तथा वैश्यः शूद्रश्चाण्डालतां व्रजेत् ॥147॥
1.216.m: A brahmin falls into the state of a śūdra, a kṣatriya becomes a crow, / a vaiśya is born [likewise as an animal], and a śūdra becomes an outcaste.

1.216.s:
tasmātpūjyo nṛpaśreṣṭha prathamaṃ vācako budhaiḥ ..
āpatkāle ca vṛddhau ca yataścāsau guruḥ smṛtaḥ .. 148 ..
1.216.d:
तस्मात्पूज्यो नृपश्रेष्ठ प्रथमं वाचको बुधैः ॥
आपत्काले च वृद्धौ च यतश्चासौ गुरुः स्मृतः ॥ 148 ॥
1.216.m: Therefore, O best of kings, the reciter is to be honored first by the wise / in times of distress and in prosperity, because he is considered a guru.

1.216.s:
vaiśākhyāmayane vīra tṛtīyāyāṃ ca suvrata ..
kārttikyāmatha mārgyāṃ ca saṃpūjyaḥ prathamaṃ bhavet .. 149 ..
1.216.d:
वैशाख्यामयने वीर तृतीयायां च सुव्रत ॥
कार्त्तिक्यामथ मार्ग्यां च संपूज्यः प्रथमं भवेत् ॥ 149 ॥
1.216.m: On the full moon day of Vaiśākha, at a solstice, O hero, and on the third lunar day, O you of good vows, / on the full moon day of Kārttika and on that of Mārgaśīrṣa, he should be honored first.

1.216.s:
parvasvanyeṣu ca vibho saṃpūjyo dharmataḥ smṛtaḥ ..
hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ ca dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ tathaiva ca .. 1.216.150 ..
1.216.d:
पर्वस्वन्येषु च विभो संपूज्यो धर्मतः स्मृतः ॥
हिरण्यं च सुवर्णं च धनं धान्यं तथैव च ॥ 1.216.150 ॥
1.216.m: And on other sacred days, O lord, he is traditionally honored according to duty. / Unrefined gold, purified gold, wealth, and likewise grain,

1.216.s:
annaṃ cāpi tathā pakvaṃ māṃsaṃ ca kurunaṃdana ..
dātavyaṃ prathamaṃ tasmai śrāvakairnṛpasattama .. 151 ..
1.216.d:
अन्नं चापि तथा पक्वं मांसं च कुरुनंदन ॥
दातव्यं प्रथमं तस्मै श्रावकैर्नृपसत्तम ॥ 151 ॥
1.216.m: as well as cooked food and meat, O joy of the Kurus, / should first be given to him by the listeners, O best of kings.

1.216.s:
vācakastu yathā nityaṃ sukhamāste narādhipa ..
na pīḍyate yathā dvaṃdvaistathā kāryaṃ varānana .. 152 ..
1.216.d:
वाचकस्तु यथा नित्यं सुखमास्ते नराधिप ॥
न पीड्यते यथा द्वंद्वैस्तथा कार्यं वरानन ॥ 152 ॥
1.216.m: In such a way that the reciter always lives comfortably, O lord of men, / and is not afflicted by the pairs of opposites, so it should be done, O fair-faced one.

1.216.s:
hemaṃte lomaśā deyāśchatraṃ prāvṛṣi sattama ..
upānahau kālayogye kāle caivānulomaśaḥ ..153..
1.216.d:
हेमंते लोमशा देयाश्छत्रं प्रावृषि सत्तम ॥
उपानहौ कालयोग्ये काले चैवानुलोमशः ॥153॥
1.216.m: Woollen blankets should be given in the cold season, an umbrella in the rainy season, O best one, / and shoes suitable for the season, in due order with the seasons.

1.216.s:
itthaṃ dvaṃdvavinirmuktaḥ sa yeṣāṃ vācako nṛpa ..
te dhanyāḥ śrāvakā loke te gatāḥ paramaṃ padam .. 154 ..
1.216.d:
इत्थं द्वंद्वविनिर्मुक्तः स येषां वाचको नृप ॥
ते धन्याः श्रावका लोके ते गताः परमं पदम् ॥ 154 ॥
1.216.m: In this way, those whose reciter is freed from the pairs of opposites, O king, / those listeners are blessed in the world, they attain the highest state.

1.216.s:
ātmanā tu kathaṃ vīra sukhamicchedvicakṣaṇaḥ ..
viṣamasthe gurau rājanyataśca sa guruḥ smṛtaḥ .. 155 ..
1.216.d:
आत्मना तु कथं वीर सुखमिच्छेद्विचक्षणः ॥
विषमस्थे गुरौ राजन्यतश्च स गुरुः स्मृतः ॥ 155 ॥
1.216.m: How could a discerning man desire happiness for himself, O hero, / when the guru is in distress, O king? For he is recognized as the guru.

1.216.s:
vācakaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca tasmāddvaṃdvaṃ vighātayet ..
yatnaḥ kāryaḥ śrāvakaiśca vācakasya janādhipa .. 156 ..
1.216.d:
वाचकश्रावकाणां च तस्माद्द्वंद्वं विघातयेत् ॥
यत्नः कार्यः श्रावकैश्च वाचकस्य जनाधिप ॥ 156 ॥
1.216.m: Therefore, [distress from] the pairs of opposites of reciters and listeners should be eliminated; / effort should be made by the listeners on behalf of the reciter, O ruler of people.

1.216.s:
itthaṃ pūjyaḥ sadā vyāsaḥ śreyo'rthaṃ prathamaṃ nṛpa ..
bhartā pūjyo yathā strīṇāṃ sarvāsāṃ vai mahī pate .. 157 ..
1.216.d:
इत्थं पूज्यः सदा व्यासः श्रेयोऽर्थं प्रथमं नृप ॥
भर्ता पूज्यो यथा स्त्रीणां सर्वासां वै मही पते ॥ 157 ॥
1.216.m: Thus a Vyāsa is always to be honored first for the sake of welfare, O king. / Just as a husband is to be honored by all women, O lord of the earth,

1.216.s:
śrāvakāṇāṃ tathā rājanvācakaḥ pūjya ucyate ..
upādhyāyastu śiṣyāṇāṃ yathā bhāgavato hariḥ .. 158 ..
1.216.d:
श्रावकाणां तथा राजन्वाचकः पूज्य उच्यते ॥
उपाध्यायस्तु शिष्याणां यथा भागवतो हरिः ॥ 158 ॥
1.216.m: so the reciter is said to be worthy of honor by listeners, O king. / Just as an instructor is to students, just as Hari is to the Bhāgavatas,

1.216.s:
saurāṇāṃ ca yathā bhānuḥ śaivānāṃ śaṃkaro yathā ..
vācakastu tathā pūjyaḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ narādhipa .. 159 ..
1.216.d:
सौराणां च यथा भानुः शैवानां शंकरो यथा ॥
वाचकस्तु तथा पूज्यः श्रावकाणां नराधिप ॥ 159 ॥
1.216.m: just as the sun is to the Sauras, just as Śaṅkara is to the Śaivas, / even so is the reciter to be honored by the listeners, O ruler of men.

1.216.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ dadatā nityaṃ śrotavyaṃ bhūtimicchatā ..
pūrvoktamāṣakaṃ tasmai vācakāya janādhipa .. 1.216.160 ..
1.216.d:
दक्षिणां ददता नित्यं श्रोतव्यं भूतिमिच्छता ॥
पूर्वोक्तमाषकं तस्मै वाचकाय जनाधिप ॥ 1.216.160 ॥
1.216.m: Constantly giving the priestly gift, one desiring prosperity must listen, / [giving] the aforesaid māṣaka to that reciter, O ruler of people.

1.216.s:
yadā dātuṃ na śaknoti māṣakaṃ kāṃcanasya tu ..
rajatasya tadā deyaṃ māṣakaṃ śreyase nṛpa .. 161 ..
1.216.d:
यदा दातुं न शक्नोति माषकं कांचनस्य तु ॥
रजतस्य तदा देयं माषकं श्रेयसे नृप ॥ 161 ॥
1.216.m: When one is unable to give a māṣaka of gold, / then a māṣaka of silver should be given for spiritual welfare, O king.

1.216.s:
tadabhāve hiraṇyaṃ ca vittaśāṭhyavivarjitaḥ ..
mṛttikāpi hi dātavyā prāpnoti satphalaṃ śubham .. 162 ..
1.216.d:
तदभावे हिरण्यं च वित्तशाठ्यविवर्जितः ॥
मृत्तिकापि हि दातव्या प्राप्नोति सत्फलं शुभम् ॥ 162 ॥
1.216.m: In its absence, [whatever] gold [one has], free from deceit regarding wealth; / even earth indeed should be given; one obtains a good, auspicious fruit.

1.216.s:
ityeṣā dakṣiṇā nityā māsimāsi bhavennṛpa ..
naimittikā bhavedrājangrahaṇādiṣu parvasu .. 163 ..
1.216.d:
इत्येषा दक्षिणा नित्या मासिमासि भवेन्नृप ॥
नैमित्तिका भवेद्राजन्ग्रहणादिषु पर्वसु ॥ 163 ॥
1.216.m: Such is the regular priestly gift, to be given month by month, O king; / and the occasional one occurs, O king, at sacred occasions such as eclipses.

1.216.s:
amale vāsasī rājangaṃdhamālyavibhūṣaṇe ..
samāpte parvaṇi vibho dātavye bhūtimicchatā .. .. 164 ..
1.216.d:
अमले वाससी राजन्गंधमाल्यविभूषणे ॥
समाप्ते पर्वणि विभो दातव्ये भूतिमिच्छता ॥ ॥ 164 ॥
1.216.m: Two spotless garments, O king, perfumes, garlands, and ornaments, / when the festival day concludes, O lord, should be given by one desiring prosperity.

1.216.s:
jñātvā sarvasamāptiṃ tu pūjayecchrāvako dhuvam ..
ātmānamapi vikrīya ya icchetsaphalaṃ śrutam .. 165 ..
1.216.d:
ज्ञात्वा सर्वसमाप्तिं तु पूजयेच्छ्रावको धुवम् ॥
आत्मानमपि विक्रीय य इच्छेत्सफलं श्रुतम् ॥ 165 ॥
1.216.m: Recognizing the complete conclusion of everything, a listener must surely worship [him], / even selling himself, if he desires the recitation heard to bear fruit.

1.216.s:
naimittikāṃ ca nityāṃ ca dakṣi ṇāmapradāya ca ..
śṛṇoti ca sadā yastu tasya tanniṣphalaṃ śrutam .. 166 ..
1.216.d:
नैमित्तिकां च नित्यां च दक्षि णामप्रदाय च ॥
शृणोति च सदा यस्तु तस्य तन्निष्फलं श्रुतम् ॥ 166 ॥
1.216.m: Without offering both the occasional and regular priestly gift, / he who always listens—to him that recitation heard is fruitless.

1.216.s:
yathā ca dakṣiṇāhīnādyajñānna phalamaśnute ..
tathā śrutaṃ ca rājeṃdra dakṣi ṇārahitaṃ smṛtam .. 167 ..
1.216.d:
यथा च दक्षिणाहीनाद्यज्ञान्न फलमश्नुते ॥
तथा श्रुतं च राजेंद्र दक्षि णारहितं स्मृतम् ॥ 167 ॥
1.216.m: And just as one does not enjoy the fruit from a sacrifice devoid of priestly gifts, / even so that which is heard without a priestly gift is traditionally regarded, O king of kings.

1.216.s:
caturguṇā bhavedrājanyā nityā dakṣiṇā vibho ..
samāpte parvaṇi vibho ityāha bhagavāñchivaḥ .. 168 ..
1.216.d:
चतुर्गुणा भवेद्राजन्या नित्या दक्षिणा विभो ॥
समाप्ते पर्वणि विभो इत्याह भगवाञ्छिवः ॥ 168 ॥
1.216.m: O king, the daily honorarium becomes fourfold, O mighty one, / when the festival is concluded, O mighty one; thus spoke the blessed Śiva.

1.216.s:
ityeṣa kathito rājanpurāṇaśravaṇe vidhiḥ ..
yataśca vidhihīnaṃ tu na karmaphalamudyate .. 169 ..
1.216.d:
इत्येष कथितो राजन्पुराणश्रवणे विधिः ॥
यतश्च विधिहीनं तु न कर्मफलमुद्यते ॥ 169 ॥
1.216.m: Thus has the rule for listening to a Purāṇa been told, O king, / since an action devoid of rule is not said to yield any fruit.

1.216.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ japo homaḥ pitṛdevābhipūjanam ..
vidhipūrvaṃ smṛtaṃ jñeyaṃ yatheha kurunadana..1.216.170 ..
1.216.d:
स्नानं दानं जपो होमः पितृदेवाभिपूजनम् ॥
विधिपूर्वं स्मृतं ज्ञेयं यथेह कुरुनदन॥1.216.170 ॥
1.216.m: Bathing, gifting, recitation of mantras, oblation into fire, and the worship of ancestors and deities / should be known as traditionally performed according to rule, just as here, O joy of the Kurus.

1.216.s:
phaladaṃ nṛpaśārdūla purāṇaśravaṇaṃ tathā ..
yathāyaṃ kathitaṃ tubhyaṃ vidhinā śravaṇaṃ mayā ..171..
1.216.d:
फलदं नृपशार्दूल पुराणश्रवणं तथा ॥
यथायं कथितं तुभ्यं विधिना श्रवणं मया ॥171॥
1.216.m: So too, listening to a Purāṇa bears fruit, O tiger among kings, / just as this listening was told to you by me according to rule.

1.216.s:
yathoktaṃ tu yathā jīvaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmavādinā ..
sa brāhmaṇo mahārāja sarvalokeṣu pūjitaḥ .. 172 ..
1.216.d:
यथोक्तं तु यथा जीवं यथोक्तं ब्रह्मवादिना ॥
स ब्राह्मणो महाराज सर्वलोकेषु पूजितः ॥ 172 ॥
1.216.m: As stated [in the scriptures], according to one's livelihood, and as spoken by a knower of the Veda, / that Brahmin, O great king, is worshipped in all worlds.

1.216.s:
yathāśrutaṃ mahābāho tathedaṃ kathitaṃ tava ..
bhāskarasya tu māhātmyaṃ māhātmyaṃ vācakasya tu .. 173 ..
1.216.d:
यथाश्रुतं महाबाहो तथेदं कथितं तव ॥
भास्करस्य तु माहात्म्यं माहात्म्यं वाचकस्य तु ॥ 173 ॥
1.216.m: Just as it was heard, O mighty-armed one, so has this been told to you: / the majesty of the Sun, and the majesty of the reciter;

1.216.s:
tathā ca saptamīkalpaḥ sarvapāpabhayāpahaḥ ..
anena vidhinā yastu pūjayetsatataṃ naraḥ .. 174 ..
1.216.d:
तथा च सप्तमीकल्पः सर्वपापभयापहः ॥
अनेन विधिना यस्तु पूजयेत्सततं नरः ॥ 174 ॥
1.216.m: and likewise the ritual manual for the seventh lunar day, which removes all sins and fears. / A person who constantly worships according to this rule,

1.216.s:
bhagalokaṃ samāsādya triṣu lokeṣu gīyate ..
tato'rkalokamāsādya gaccheccitraśikhaṃḍinaḥ .. 175 ..
1.216.d:
भगलोकं समासाद्य त्रिषु लोकेषु गीयते ॥
ततोऽर्कलोकमासाद्य गच्छेच्चित्रशिखंडिनः ॥ 175 ॥
1.216.m: reaching the realm of Bhaga, is celebrated throughout the three worlds. / Then, reaching the realm of the Sun, he would go to the Citraśikhaṇḍins;

1.216.s:
tasmādapi mahābāho gacchellokaṃ divākaram..
arkaloke tato yātastato golokamaśnute .. 176 ..
1.216.d:
तस्मादपि महाबाहो गच्छेल्लोकं दिवाकरम्॥
अर्कलोके ततो यातस्ततो गोलोकमश्नुते ॥ 176 ॥
1.216.m: from there too, O mighty-armed one, he would go to the realm of the Sun. / Having gone from the realm of the Sun, he then attains the realm of cows;

1.216.s:
ṛtasya ca tato gacchetkaṃjajasya tataḥ param ..
daśānāṃ rājasūyānāmagniṣṭomaśatasya ca .. 177 ..
1.216.d:
ऋतस्य च ततो गच्छेत्कंजजस्य ततः परम् ॥
दशानां राजसूयानामग्निष्टोमशतस्य च ॥ 177 ॥
1.216.m: and then he would go to the [realm] of Ṛta, and thereafter to that of the Lotus-born. / Of ten royal consecrations and of a hundred Agniṣṭoma sacrifices,

1.216.s:
śravaṇātphalamāpnoti pitāmahavaco yathā .. 178 ..
.. pūrvārdhaḥ samāpto'yam ..
.. śrīnārāyaṇārpaṇamastu .. ..
ayaṃ yunikoḍa rūpāntaraṇaṃ āśvin śukla saptamī, vikrama saṃvat 2073 tithau indsenz OCR dvārā nimnalikhita pustakadvayebhyaḥ kṛtamasti -
śrībhaviṣyapurāṇam(nāga prakāśaka, dillī)
śrībhaviṣyapurāṇam (hindī sāhitya sammelana, prayāga)
1.216.d:
श्रवणात्फलमाप्नोति पितामहवचो यथा ॥ 178 ॥
॥ पूर्वार्धः समाप्तोऽयम् ॥
॥ श्रीनारायणार्पणमस्तु ॥ ॥
अयं युनिकोड रूपान्तरणं आश्विन् शुक्ल सप्तमी, विक्रम संवत् 2073 तिथौ इन्द्सेन्z ओच्र् द्वारा निम्नलिखित पुस्तकद्वयेभ्यः कृतमस्ति -
श्रीभविष्यपुराणम्(नाग प्रकाशक, दिल्ली)
श्रीभविष्यपुराणम् (हिन्दी साहित्य सम्मेलन, प्रयाग)
1.216.m:
he obtains the fruit from listening, according to the word of the Grandfather.
This first half is concluded.
May it be dedicated to the blessed Nārāyaṇa.

1.217.s: prathama - adhyāya saṃkhyā, dvitīya - pṛṣṭha saṃkhyā
1.217.d: प्रथम - अध्याय संख्या, द्वितीय - पृष्ठ संख्या
1.217.m: First: chapter number; second: page number.

1.217.s: 1 1 śatānīko vyāsaṃ cāturvarṇyadharmaṃ cāturvarṇyabhavaṇayogyadharmādyākhyānañca śrotuṃ papraccha sa ca tvāṃ sumantuḥ śrāvayiṣyatītyavocat . tataḥ śatānīkena pṛṣṭena sumantunā purāṇānāṃ pāpahāritvamupapādya viśeṣato bhaviṣyapurāṇapraśaṃsā paraṃparayā purāṇapravartanaṃ tadīyapadyasaṃkhyāvaṇarnañca ślo0 106
1.217.d: 1 1 शतानीको व्यासं चातुर्वर्ण्यधर्मं चातुर्वर्ण्यभवणयोग्यधर्माद्याख्यानञ्च श्रोतुं पप्रच्छ स च त्वां सुमन्तुः श्रावयिष्यतीत्यवोचत् । ततः शतानीकेन पृष्टेन सुमन्तुना पुराणानां पापहारित्वमुपपाद्य विशेषतो भविष्यपुराणप्रशंसा परंपरया पुराणप्रवर्तनं तदीयपद्यसंख्यावणर्नञ्च श्लो0 106
1.217.m: 1 1 Śatānīka asked Vyāsa to hear the duty of the four classes and the narrative of duties suitable for the dwelling of the four classes, and he said, “Sumantu will recite it to you.” Then, upon being asked by Śatānīka, Sumantu established that the Purāṇas remove sins, especially praised the Bhaviṣyapurāṇa, and described the transmission of the Purāṇa through tradition and the number of its verses. Verses: 106.
2 3 Description of creation, and description of the origin of the Purāṇas from the fifth month of Brahmā. Verses: 173.
3 7 Description in brief of all life-cycle rites beginning with conception, and description of the rules for sipping water and other rites. Verses: 95.
4 9 Description of the rule for the sacred thread investiture preceded by the description of the majesty of the Sāvitrī along with the description of the meaning of the syllable Oṃ. Verses: 222.
5 13 Description of the auspicious and inauspicious bodily marks of women. Verses: 111.
6 15 Account of the duty of acquiring wealth for householders preceded by the account of auspicious bodily marks and virtuous conduct of women. Verses: 44.
7 16 Description of the rules of marriage. Verses: 68.
8 18 Description of human conduct preceded by the examination of the vicious and non-vicious nature of women and the account of proper conduct toward them. Verses: 72.
9 19 Praise of the traditional texts preceded by what is to be done by women. Verses: 17.
10 20 Description of the wicked conduct of women. Verses: 22.
11 20 Description of the rule of domestic duties for women. Verses: 21.
12 21 Description of the manner of accumulating various grains, supporting dependents, gathering milk and other provisions, and timely service to one's husband to be performed by women. Verses: 57.

13 22 Description of waking before the husband, sweeping the stove and other things, cooking, inquiring into righteousness and unrighteousness concerning relatives and kin, and preserving one's own proper conduct. Verses: 66.
14 23 Description of abstaining from adornments other than auspicious ones when the husband is abroad. Verses: 12.
15 24 Description of the duties of women. Verses: 32.

16 25 Description of the attainment of Brahminhood by Viśvāmitra and others arising from the majesty of the first lunar day, preceded by the description of each observance involving milk and other items on each lunar day. Verses: 63.
17 36 Description of the worship of Brahmā in the context of the ritual manual for the first lunar day. Verses: 118.
18 28 Description of the first lunar day of Bali's kingdom. Verses: 28.

1.217.s: 19 29 dvitīyākalpe puṣpadvitīyāmāhātmyavarṇane śaryātikartṛkacyavanoddeśyakasukanyāniveda- nottarakumārakartṛkacyavanasambandhiyuvatvaprāptyuttaraṃ dasrayoścyavanakalpitayajña- bhāgabhuktvena kuddhaśakrasya taddhananāya vajrodyamanaṃ tenasaṃjātakopacyavanakartṛkendra- bhujastaṃbhavarṇanam . paścācchakrastutiprasannacyavanakartṛkaprasādena śakrasya bhujastaṃbha. nābhāvavarṇanañca ślo. 91
1.217.d: 19 29 द्वितीयाकल्पे पुष्पद्वितीयामाहात्म्यवर्णने शर्यातिकर्तृकच्यवनोद्देश्यकसुकन्यानिवेद- नोत्तरकुमारकर्तृकच्यवनसम्बन्धियुवत्वप्राप्त्युत्तरं दस्रयोश्च्यवनकल्पितयज्ञ- भागभुक्त्वेन कुद्धशक्रस्य तद्धननाय वज्रोद्यमनं तेनसंजातकोपच्यवनकर्तृकेन्द्र- भुजस्तंभवर्णनम् । पश्चाच्छक्रस्तुतिप्रसन्नच्यवनकर्तृकप्रसादेन शक्रस्य भुजस्तंभ। नाभाववर्णनञ्च श्लो। 91
1.217.m: 19 29 In the description of the majesty of the Flower-Second in the ritual manual for the second lunar day, the presentation of Sukanyā intended for Cyavana performed by Śaryāti; thereafter, Cyavana's attainment of youth performed by the Kumāras; thereafter, Indra's raising of his thunderbolt to slay Cyavana out of anger due to the two Dasras enjoying the sacrificial portion devised by Cyavana, and the description of the paralysis of Indra's arm performed by Cyavana who became enraged thereby; and subsequently, the description of the cessation of the paralysis of Śakra's arm through the favour of Cyavana who was pleased by Śakra's praise. Verses: 91.
20 31 The majesty of the observance of the Non-Empty Bed Second. Verses: 33.
21 32 Description of the rule of the ritual manual for the third lunar day. Verses: 33.

1.217.s: 22 33 caturthīkalpe kārtikeyakartṛkavināyakaviṣāṇavicchedavarṇanaṃ tathā rudrakartṛkabrahmaśi- raśchedanaṃ tatkopena brahmakṛtarudranāśārthaśvetakuṇḍalipuruṣotpattivarṇanam . tena rudra- hananāyodyatena rudranārāyaṇobhayanirmitaṣuruṣayuddhavarṇanaṃ ca. ślo 51
1.217.d: 22 33 चतुर्थीकल्पे कार्तिकेयकर्तृकविनायकविषाणविच्छेदवर्णनं तथा रुद्रकर्तृकब्रह्मशि- रश्छेदनं तत्कोपेन ब्रह्मकृतरुद्रनाशार्थश्वेतकुण्डलिपुरुषोत्पत्तिवर्णनम् । तेन रुद्र- हननायोद्यतेन रुद्रनारायणोभयनिर्मितषुरुषयुद्धवर्णनं च। श्लो 51
1.217.m: 22 33 In the ritual manual for the fourth lunar day, the description of the breaking of Vināyaka's tusk performed by Kārtikeya; likewise, the cutting off of Brahmā's head performed by Rudra, and the description of the origin of the white-earringed man produced by Brahmā out of anger for the destruction of Rudra; and the description of the battle between the men created by both Rudra and Nārāyaṇa against him who was prepared to slay Rudra. Verses: 51.

1.217.s: 23 33 caturthīkalpavarṇane bhīmajasya vighnādhikāritvavarṇanaṃ. tadarcāvidhivarṇanaṃ, tadāvara- ṇapūjāvarṇanaṃ ca ślo. 31

1.217.m: 23 33 In the description of the ritual manual for the fourth lunar day, the description of the son of Bhīma having authority over obstacles; the description of the rule for his worship, and the description of the worship of his enclosure. Verses: 31.
